source.verse_hash_method: SHA-256 of exact original XML verse substrings including written/read and other notes; no normalized reconstruction.
source.public_versification_note: 1 Samuel 17–31: 404 public verses bind to 405 exact original records. Public 1Sam 20:42 binds complete Hebrew 20:42 and 21:1; public 21:1–15 binds Hebrew 21:2–16; public 23:29 binds Hebrew 24:1; public 24:1–22 binds Hebrew 24:2–23. All other verses in this batch are one-to-one.

delta_method: F0 retained wording; F1 lexical; F2 syntax/idiom; F3 consequential interpretive, textual, social, or versification choice. Editorial choices are independent of overlap scores. No minimum-change quota. Independent review has not occurred.

verses.rationale: Makes the gathering and camp locations distinct without collapsing the place names.
verses.before: The Philistines gathered their armies for battle and were gathered at Socoh, which belongs to Judah. They camped between Socoh and Azekah, in Ephes-Dammim.
verses.after: The Philistines gathered their armies for war at Socoh in Judah. They camped between Socoh and Azekah, at Ephes-dammim.
verses.tsw_comparator: The Philistines gathered their armies for battle and were gathered at Socoh, which belongs to Judah. They camped between Socoh and Azekah, in Ephes-Dammim.

verses.rationale: Separates encampment from military formation and retains valley name.
verses.before: Saul and the men of Israel were gathered and camped in the Valley of Elah. They drew up in battle formation to meet the Philistines.
verses.after: Saul and the men of Israel gathered and camped in the Valley of Elah. They formed their battle lines facing the Philistines.
verses.tsw_comparator: Saul and the men of Israel were gathered and camped in the Valley of Elah. They drew up in battle formation to meet the Philistines.

verses.rationale: Keeps the opposing slopes and intervening valley clear.
verses.before: The Philistines stood on the mountain on one side, and Israel stood on the mountain on the other side, with the valley between them.
verses.after: The Philistines stood on one hillside and Israel on the other, with the valley between them.
verses.tsw_comparator: The Philistines stood on the mountain on one side, and Israel stood on the mountain on the other side, with the valley between them.

verses.rationale: Retains the pinned height and ancient units; champion renders the man between the armies.
verses.before: Then a champion came out from the camps of the Philistines, whose name was Goliath from Gath. His height was six cubits and a span.
verses.after: A champion came out from the Philistine camps. His name was Goliath, from Gath, and he stood six cubits and a span tall.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then a champion came out from the camps of the Philistines, whose name was Goliath from Gath. His height was six cubits and a span.

verses.rationale: Keeps the armor type, material and weight without an exact modern conversion.
verses.before: A bronze helmet was upon his head, and he was clothed with scale armor; the weight of the armor was five thousand shekels of bronze.
verses.after: He wore a bronze helmet and a coat of scale armor. The bronze armor weighed five thousand shekels.
verses.tsw_comparator: A bronze helmet was upon his head, and he was clothed with scale armor; the weight of the armor was five thousand shekels of bronze.

verses.rationale: Preserves the equipment and its position rather than merging javelin and spear.
verses.before: He had bronze greaves upon his legs and a bronze javelin between his shoulders.
verses.after: Bronze greaves covered his legs, and a bronze javelin rested between his shoulders.
verses.tsw_comparator: He had bronze greaves upon his legs and a bronze javelin between his shoulders.

verses.rationale: Follows the qere shaft and retains the textile image, iron and separate shield-bearer.
verses.before: The shaft of his spear was like a weaver’s beam, and the blade of his spear weighed six hundred shekels of iron. His shield-bearer went before him.
verses.after: His spear shaft was like a weaver’s beam, and its iron head weighed six hundred shekels. A shield-bearer walked ahead of him.
verses.tsw_comparator: The shaft of his spear was like a weaver’s beam, and the blade of his spear weighed six hundred shekels of iron. His shield-bearer went before him.

verses.rationale: Keeps the taunting contrast of the Philistine with Saul’s servants.
verses.before: He stood and called to the battle lines of Israel and said to them, “Why have you come out to arrange for battle? Am I not the Philistine, and are you not servants of Saul? Choose for yourselves a man, and let him come down to me.
verses.after: He stood and shouted to Israel’s ranks, “Why come out and form battle lines? Am I not the Philistine, and are you not Saul’s servants? Choose a man and let him come down to me.
verses.tsw_comparator: He stood and called to the battle lines of Israel and said to them, “Why have you come out to arrange for battle? Am I not the Philistine, and are you not servants of Saul? Choose for yourselves a man, and let him come down to me.

verses.rationale: Preserves both conditional outcomes and the actual enslavement at stake.
verses.before: If he can fight with me and strike me, then we will become your servants. But if I prevail against him and strike him, then you will become our servants and serve us.”
verses.after: If he can fight me and kill me, we will be your slaves. But if I defeat him and kill him, you will be our slaves and serve us.”
verses.tsw_comparator: If he is able to fight with me and strike me, then we will become your servants. But if I prevail against him and strike him, then you shall become our servants and serve us.”

verses.rationale: Carries the repeated defiance and singular combat challenge.
verses.before: The Philistine said, “I myself defy the battle lines of Israel this day. Give me a man, and let us fight together.”
verses.after: The Philistine said, “Today I defy Israel’s ranks! Give me a man, and let us fight.”
verses.tsw_comparator: The Philistine said, “I myself defy the battle lines of Israel this day. Give me a man, and let us fight together.”

verses.rationale: Preserves both dismay and intense fear in direct English.
verses.before: Saul and all Israel heard these words of the Philistine and were shattered and greatly afraid.
verses.after: When Saul and all Israel heard the Philistine’s words, they were shattered and terrified.
verses.tsw_comparator: Saul and all Israel heard these words of the Philistine and were shattered and greatly afraid.

verses.rationale: Keeps the fresh introduction and eight sons; difficult age phrase is noted.
verses.before: Now David was son of this Ephrathite man from Bethlehem in Judah, whose name was Jesse. He had eight sons, and the man in the days of Saul was old, advanced among men.
verses.after: David was the son of an Ephrathite from Bethlehem in Judah named Jesse. Jesse had eight sons and was already an old man in Saul’s time.
verses.tsw_comparator: Now David was son of this Ephrathite man from Bethlehem in Judah, whose name was Jesse. He had eight sons, and the man in the days of Saul was old, advanced among men.

verses.rationale: Keeps all three names and birth order.
verses.before: The three oldest sons of Jesse had gone after Saul to the battle. The names of his three sons who went to battle were Eliab the firstborn, Abinadab his second, and Shammah the third.
verses.after: Jesse’s three oldest sons had gone to war with Saul: Eliab the firstborn, Abinadab the second, and Shammah the third.
verses.tsw_comparator: The three oldest sons of Jesse had gone after Saul to the battle. The names of his three sons who went to battle were Eliab the firstborn, Abinadab his second, and Shammah the third.

verses.rationale: Retains the repeated age contrast and lets the sentence continue.
verses.before: David was the youngest. The three oldest had gone after Saul.
verses.after: David was the youngest. The three oldest followed Saul,
verses.tsw_comparator: David was the youngest. The three oldest had gone after Saul.

verses.rationale: Clarifies repeated travel without harmonizing the later recognition scene.
verses.before: Yet David went and returned from Saul to shepherd his father’s flock at Bethlehem.
verses.after: while David went back and forth from Saul to tend his father’s flock at Bethlehem.
verses.tsw_comparator: But David went and returned from Saul to shepherd his father’s flock at Bethlehem.

verses.rationale: Preserves duration and twice-daily challenge.
verses.before: The Philistine drew near morning and evening and presented himself forty days.
verses.after: For forty days the Philistine came forward, taking his stand morning and evening.
verses.tsw_comparator: The Philistine drew near morning and evening and presented himself forty days.

verses.rationale: Retains the grain measure, preparation and ten loaves.
verses.before: Jesse said to David his son, “Please take for your brothers an ephah of this roasted grain and these ten loaves and run to the camp to your brothers.
verses.after: Jesse told his son David, “Take this ephah of roasted grain and these ten loaves to your brothers. Hurry them to the camp.
verses.tsw_comparator: Jesse said to David his son, “Please take for your brothers an ephah of this roasted grain and these ten loaves and run to the camp to your brothers.

verses.rationale: Keeps the commander's rank and difficult pledge/token expression, flagged in a note.
verses.before: And take these ten cuts of cheese to the commander of their thousand. Visit your brothers for their well-being and take their pledge.”
verses.after: Take these ten portions of cheese to their commander of a thousand. Find out how your brothers are and bring back a token from them.
verses.tsw_comparator: And take these ten cuts of cheese to the commander of their thousand. Visit your brothers for their well-being and take their pledge.”

verses.rationale: Keeps Jesse’s explanation within his speech. The Hebrew can also be read as a return to the narrator; the note preserves this speaker uncertainty.
verses.before: Now Saul and they and all the men of Israel were in the Valley of Elah fighting with the Philistines.
verses.after: They are with Saul and all the men of Israel in the Valley of Elah, fighting the Philistines.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Now Saul and they and all the men of Israel were in the Valley of Elah fighting with the Philistines.

verses.rationale: Tracks care of flock, obedience, arrival and army movement in order.
verses.before: David rose early in the morning, left the flock with a keeper, carried the provisions, and went as Jesse had commanded him. He came to the encampment as the army was going out to the battle line and shouting for battle.
verses.after: David got up early, left the flock with a keeper, and carried off the supplies as Jesse had instructed. He reached the camp enclosure as the army was marching out to its lines, raising the battle cry.
verses.tsw_comparator: David rose early in the morning, left the flock with a keeper, carried the provisions, and went as Jesse had commanded him. He came to the encampment as the army was going out to the battle line and shouting for battle.

verses.rationale: Preserves the repeated face-to-face formation.
verses.before: Israel and the Philistines arranged battle line against battle line.
verses.after: Israel and the Philistines drew up their lines, army facing army.
verses.tsw_comparator: Israel and the Philistines arranged battle line against battle line.

verses.rationale: Distinguishes the supply keeper from the earlier shepherd.
verses.before: David left the things from upon him in the hand of the keeper of the baggage, ran to the battle line, and came and asked his brothers about their well-being.
verses.after: David left his load with the keeper of the supplies and ran to the battle line to greet his brothers.
verses.tsw_comparator: David left the things from upon him in the hand of the keeper of the baggage, ran to the battle line, and came and asked his brothers about their well-being.

verses.rationale: Follows qere ranks and retains repeated identification and David’s hearing.
verses.before: As he was speaking with them, look, the champion, Goliath the Philistine from Gath, came up from the battle lines of the Philistines and spoke according to these words, and David heard.
verses.after: As he spoke with them, the champion came up from the Philistine ranks—Goliath, the Philistine from Gath. He repeated his challenge, and David heard it.
verses.tsw_comparator: As he was speaking with them, behold, the champion, Goliath the Philistine from Gath, came up from the battle lines of the Philistines and spoke according to these words, and David heard.

verses.rationale: Renders collective Israelite men naturally while retaining flight.
verses.before: When all the men of Israel saw the man, they fled from before him and were greatly afraid.
verses.after: Whenever the Israelites saw the man, they fled from him in terror.
verses.tsw_comparator: When all the men of Israel saw the man, they fled from before him and were greatly afraid.

verses.rationale: Preserves reported rewards and qualifies the undefined household exemption in a note.
verses.before: The men of Israel said, “Have you seen this man who comes up? Surely he comes up to defy Israel. And it will be that the man who strikes him, the king will enrich him with great riches, give him his daughter, and make his father’s house free in Israel.”
verses.after: The Israelites were saying, “Have you seen this man coming up? He comes to defy Israel. The king will make the man who kills him very rich, give him his daughter, and free his father’s household from obligations in Israel.”
verses.tsw_comparator: The men of Israel said, “Have you seen this man who comes up? Surely he comes up to defy Israel. And it shall be that the man who strikes him, the king will enrich him with great riches, give him his daughter, and make his father’s house free in Israel.”

verses.rationale: Keeps David’s reward question, covenant marker and living-God challenge together.
verses.before: David spoke to the men standing with him, saying, “What will be done for the man who strikes this Philistine and removes reproach from Israel? For who is this uncircumcised Philistine that he should defy the battle lines of the living God?”
verses.after: David asked the men standing near him, “What will be done for the man who kills this Philistine and removes Israel’s disgrace? Who is this uncircumcised Philistine, that he should defy the ranks of the living God?”
verses.tsw_comparator: David spoke to the men standing with him, saying, “What will be done for the man who strikes this Philistine and removes reproach from Israel? For who is this uncircumcised Philistine that he should defy the battle lines of the living God?”

verses.rationale: Preserves repeated response without inventing a second reward list.
verses.before: The people spoke to him according to this word, saying, “Thus will it be done for the man who strikes him.”
verses.after: They repeated what they had said about the reward for the man who killed him.
verses.tsw_comparator: The people spoke to him according to this word, saying, “Thus shall it be done for the man who strikes him.”

verses.rationale: Keeps Eliab’s accusations as his words and retains the belittling few sheep.
verses.before: Eliab his oldest brother heard when he spoke to the men, and Eliab’s anger burned against David. He said, “Why did you come down? And with whom did you leave those few sheep in the wilderness? I know your presumption and the evil of your heart, for you came down so that you might see the battle.”
verses.after: His oldest brother Eliab heard him talking with the men and grew angry. “Why have you come down here? Who did you leave those few sheep with in the wilderness? I know your arrogance and your wicked heart. You came down to watch the battle!”
verses.tsw_comparator: Eliab his oldest brother heard when he spoke to the men, and Eliab’s anger burned against David. He said, “Why did you come down? And with whom did you leave those few sheep in the wilderness? I know your presumption and the evil of your heart, for you came down so that you might see the battle.”

verses.rationale: Renders the terse word/question idiom; alternative force remains in the note.
verses.before: David said, “What have I done now? Was it not only a word?”
verses.after: David answered, “What have I done now? Can I not ask a question?”
verses.tsw_comparator: David said, “What have I done now? Was it not only a word?”

verses.rationale: Retains the repeated inquiry and answer without adding David’s motive.
verses.before: He turned from beside him toward another and spoke according to the same word, and the people returned a word to him like the former word.
verses.after: He turned away to someone else and asked the same thing. The people answered as before.
verses.tsw_comparator: He turned from beside him toward another and spoke according to the same word, and the people returned a word to him like the former word.

verses.rationale: Clarifies the passive report and Saul’s agency.
verses.before: The words that David spoke were heard, and they reported them before Saul, and he sent for him.
verses.after: What David said was overheard and reported to Saul, who sent for him.
verses.tsw_comparator: The words that David spoke were heard, and they reported them before Saul, and he sent for him.

verses.rationale: Retains heart idiom and David’s self-designation as servant.
verses.before: David said to Saul, “Let no human heart fall because of him. Your servant will go and fight with this Philistine.”
verses.after: David told Saul, “Let no one lose heart because of him. Your servant will go and fight this Philistine.”
verses.tsw_comparator: David said to Saul, “Let no human heart fall because of him. Your servant will go and fight with this Philistine.”

verses.rationale: Keeps the pointed comparison of youth with lifelong fighting experience.
verses.before: Saul said to David, “You are not able to go against this Philistine to fight with him, for you are a youth, and he is a man of war from his youth.”
verses.after: Saul answered, “You cannot go and fight this Philistine. You are only a boy, and he has been a warrior since he was young.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Saul said to David, “You are not able to go against this Philistine to fight with him, for you are a youth, and he is a man of war from his youth.”

verses.rationale: Preserves the shepherd’s recurring experience and carries the conditional narrative onward.
verses.before: David said to Saul, “Your servant was shepherding his father’s flock, and a lion came, and also a bear, and carried off a sheep from the flock.
verses.after: David said, “Your servant has tended his father’s flock. When a lion or a bear came and carried off a sheep,
verses.tsw_comparator: David said to Saul, “Your servant was shepherding his father’s flock, and a lion came, and also a bear, and carried off a sheep from the flock.

verses.rationale: Retains the unusual beard image and all actions in the rescue.
verses.before: I went out after it and struck it and rescued from its mouth. When it rose against me, I seized it by its beard, struck it, and put it to death.
verses.after: I went after it, struck it, and rescued the sheep from its mouth. If it turned on me, I caught it by the beard, struck it, and killed it.
verses.tsw_comparator: I went out after it and struck it and rescued from its mouth. When it rose against me, I seized it by its beard, struck it, and put it to death.

verses.rationale: Preserves both animals, repeated defiance and the comparison.
verses.before: Your servant struck both lion and bear, and this uncircumcised Philistine will be like one of them, because he defied the battle lines of the living God.”
verses.after: Your servant has killed both lion and bear. This uncircumcised Philistine will be like one of them, because he has defied the ranks of the living God.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Your servant struck both lion and bear, and this uncircumcised Philistine shall be like one of them, because he defied the battle lines of the living God.”

verses.rationale: Preserves repeated rescue and hand/paw imagery with an audible speaker change.
verses.before: David said, “The LORD who rescued me from the paw of the lion and from the paw of the bear, he will rescue me from the hand of this Philistine.” Saul said to David, “Go, and may the LORD be with you.”
verses.after: David added, “The LORD rescued me from the paw of the lion and the paw of the bear. He will rescue me from this Philistine’s hand.” Saul said, “Go, and may the LORD be with you.”
verses.tsw_comparator: David said, “The LORD who rescued me from the paw of the lion and from the paw of the bear, he will rescue me from the hand of this Philistine.” Saul said to David, “Go, and may the LORD be with you.”

verses.rationale: Keeps Saul’s personal gear and the sequence of dressing.
verses.before: Saul clothed David with his garments, put a bronze helmet upon his head, and clothed him with armor.
verses.after: Saul dressed David in his own gear. He put a bronze helmet on his head and fitted him with armor.
verses.tsw_comparator: Saul clothed David with his garments, put a bronze helmet upon his head, and clothed him with armor.

verses.rationale: Preserves repeated lack of testing without asserting armor weight as the cause.
verses.before: David strapped his sword over his garments and tried to walk, for he had not tested them. David said to Saul, “I am not able to walk with these, for I have not tested them.” So David removed them from himself.
verses.after: David strapped Saul’s sword over the gear and tried to walk, for he had never tested it. “I cannot walk in this,” he told Saul. “I have not tried it before.” So David took it off.
verses.tsw_comparator: David strapped his sword over his garments and tried to walk, for he had not tested them. David said to Saul, “I am not able to walk with these, for I have not tested them.” So David removed them from himself.

verses.rationale: Keeps five stones, wadi and equipment; does not modernize sling into slingshot.
verses.before: He took his staff in his hand, chose for himself five smooth stones from the wadi, and put them in the shepherd’s bag that he had, in the pouch. His sling was in his hand, and he drew near to the Philistine.
verses.after: He took his staff and chose five smooth stones from the wadi, putting them in his shepherd’s bag, in its pouch. With his sling in hand, he approached the Philistine.
verses.tsw_comparator: He took his staff in his hand, chose for himself five smooth stones from the wadi, and put them in the shepherd’s bag that he had, in the pouch. His sling was in his hand, and he drew near to the Philistine.

verses.rationale: Retains continuing approach and shield-bearer position.
verses.before: The Philistine came on, drawing nearer to David, and the man carrying the shield was before him.
verses.after: The Philistine kept coming closer to David, with his shield-bearer in front.
verses.tsw_comparator: The Philistine came on, drawing nearer to David, and the man carrying the shield was before him.

verses.rationale: Preserves contempt and the source’s explicit description of appearance.
verses.before: The Philistine looked and saw David and despised him, for he was a youth, ruddy, and handsome in appearance.
verses.after: He looked David over and despised him: he was just a boy, ruddy and handsome.
verses.tsw_comparator: The Philistine looked and saw David and despised him, for he was a youth, ruddy, and handsome in appearance.

verses.rationale: Keeps the dog insult, plural sticks and divine invocation as reported speech.
verses.before: The Philistine said to David, “Am I a dog, that you come to me with sticks?” And the Philistine cursed David by his gods.
verses.after: The Philistine said to David, “Am I a dog, that you come at me with sticks?” Then he cursed David by his gods.
verses.tsw_comparator: The Philistine said to David, “Am I a dog, that you come to me with sticks?” And the Philistine cursed David by his gods.

verses.rationale: Preserves the bodily threat and both animal groups.
verses.before: The Philistine said to David, “Come to me, and I will give your flesh to the birds of the heavens and to the animals of the field.”
verses.after: “Come here,” he said, “and I will give your flesh to the birds of the sky and the beasts of the field!”
verses.tsw_comparator: The Philistine said to David, “Come to me, and I will give your flesh to the birds of the heavens and to the animals of the field.”

verses.rationale: Keeps three weapons and the repeated defiance against divine authority.
verses.before: David said to the Philistine, “You come to me with sword, spear, and javelin, but I come to you in the name of the LORD of Hosts, the God of the battle lines of Israel, whom you have defied.
verses.after: David answered, “You come at me with sword, spear, and javelin. I come at you in the name of the LORD of Armies, the God of Israel’s ranks, whom you have defied.
verses.tsw_comparator: David said to the Philistine, “You come to me with sword, spear, and javelin, but I come to you in the name of the LORD of Hosts, the God of the battle lines of Israel, whom you have defied.

verses.rationale: Retains beheading, corpses and worldwide recognition without softening violence.
verses.before: This day the LORD will give you into my hand, and I will strike you and remove your head from you. I will give the corpses of the camp of the Philistines this day to the birds of the heavens and to the wild animals of the earth, so that all the earth may know that there is a God in Israel.
verses.after: Today the LORD will hand you over to me. I will strike you down and cut off your head. Today I will give the bodies of the Philistine army to the birds of the sky and the beasts of the earth. Then the whole earth will know that Israel has a God.
verses.tsw_comparator: This day the LORD will give you into my hand, and I will strike you and remove your head from you. I will give the corpses of the camp of the Philistines this day to the birds of the heavens and to the wild animals of the earth, so that all the earth may know that there is a God in Israel.

verses.rationale: Preserves contrast with weapons and movement from singular opponent to plural enemies.
verses.before: And all this assembly will know that the LORD does not save by sword and spear, for the battle belongs to the LORD, and he will give you into our hand.”
verses.after: Everyone gathered here will know that the LORD does not save by sword or spear. The battle belongs to the LORD, and he will hand you over to us.”
verses.tsw_comparator: And all this assembly shall know that the LORD does not save by sword and spear, for the battle belongs to the LORD, and he will give you into our hand.”

verses.rationale: Keeps David’s speed against the opponent’s advance.
verses.before: And it happened when the Philistine arose and went and drew near to meet David that David hurried and ran toward the battle line to meet the Philistine.
verses.after: As the Philistine moved forward to meet him, David hurried toward the battle line and ran to meet the Philistine.
verses.tsw_comparator: And it happened when the Philistine arose and went and drew near to meet David that David hurried and ran toward the battle line to meet the Philistine.

verses.rationale: Retains the stone sinking into the forehead and direction of collapse.
verses.before: David stretched his hand into the bag, took from there a stone, slung it, and struck the Philistine on his forehead. The stone sank into his forehead, and he fell upon his face to the ground.
verses.after: David reached into his bag, took a stone, and slung it. It struck the Philistine in the forehead and sank in. He fell facedown to the ground.
verses.tsw_comparator: David stretched his hand into the bag, took from there a stone, slung it, and struck the Philistine on his forehead. The stone sank into his forehead, and he fell upon his face to the ground.

verses.rationale: Keeps the summary death statement without harmonizing it with verse 51.
verses.before: So David prevailed over the Philistine with sling and stone. He struck the Philistine and put him to death, though there was no sword in David’s hand.
verses.after: So David overpowered the Philistine with a sling and a stone. He struck him down and killed him, though David had no sword in his hand.
verses.tsw_comparator: So David prevailed over the Philistine with sling and stone. He struck the Philistine and put him to death, though there was no sword in David’s hand.

verses.rationale: Retains repeated killing and beheading rather than silently rewriting the sequence.
verses.before: Then David ran, stood over the Philistine, took his sword, drew it from its sheath, put him to death, and cut off his head with it. When the Philistines saw that their champion was dead, they fled.
verses.after: David ran and stood over him. He took the Philistine’s sword, drew it from its sheath, and killed him, cutting off his head with it. When the Philistines saw that their champion was dead, they fled.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then David ran, stood over the Philistine, took his sword, drew it from its sheath, put him to death, and cut off his head with it. When the Philistines saw that their champion was dead, they fled.

verses.rationale: Keeps the pinned valley reading and named route; textual question noted.
verses.before: The men of Israel and Judah arose and shouted and pursued the Philistines as far as the entrance of the valley and as far as the gates of Ekron. The slain Philistines fell on the way of Shaaraim as far as Gath and Ekron.
verses.after: The men of Israel and Judah rose with a shout and pursued the Philistines as far as the entrance to the valley and the gates of Ekron. Philistine bodies lay along the road to Shaaraim, all the way to Gath and Ekron.
verses.tsw_comparator: The men of Israel and Judah arose and shouted and pursued the Philistines as far as the entrance of the valley and as far as the gates of Ekron. The slain Philistines fell on the way of Shaaraim as far as Gath and Ekron.

verses.rationale: Distinguishes pursuit from subsequent plunder.
verses.before: The children of Israel returned from hotly pursuing the Philistines and plundered their camps.
verses.after: After chasing the Philistines, the Israelites returned and plundered their camps.
verses.tsw_comparator: The children of Israel returned from hotly pursuing the Philistines and plundered their camps.

verses.rationale: Retains Jerusalem without supplying an unrecorded date or harmonization.
verses.before: David took the head of the Philistine and brought it to Jerusalem, but he put his weapons in his tent.
verses.after: David took the Philistine’s head to Jerusalem and put his weapons in his own tent.

verses.rationale: Marks the narrative’s return to the earlier moment and preserves the father question.

verses.after: The king said, “Find out whose son the young man is.”
verses.tsw_comparator: The king said, “You inquire whose son this youth is.”

verses.rationale: Retains the precise familial answer and servant designation.

verses.rationale: Preserves the binding of lives and unqualified love, without assigning a modern relationship category.

verses.after: When David finished speaking with Saul, Jonathan’s life became bound to David’s life, and Jonathan loved him as himself.

verses.rationale: Makes Saul’s control and denied return explicit.

verses.after: Saul kept David with him that day and would not let him return to his father’s house.
verses.tsw_comparator: Saul took him that day and would not let him return to his father’s house.

verses.rationale: Keeps covenant and the repeated reason of love.

verses.after: Jonathan made a covenant with David because he loved him as himself.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Jonathan made a covenant with David, because he loved him as his own soul.

verses.rationale: Retains every transferred item without adding a formal abdication claim.

verses.rationale: Uses success for prudent action here while keeping the public and court responses.

verses.rationale: Retains women meeting Saul and qualifies the uncertain instrument by a note.

verses.rationale: Keeps Saul’s attribution language and fear of kingship.

verses.rationale: Renders the qere eyeing idiom while preserving the eye image.

verses.rationale: Retains the same prophesying verb rather than silently diagnosing Saul; contextual ambiguity noted.

verses.rationale: Makes both names explicit to prevent reversed referents.

verses.tsw_comparator: Saul was afraid of David, because the LORD was with him but had departed from Saul.

verses.rationale: Keeps removal, rank and the going-out/coming-in leadership image.

verses.rationale: Preserves the paired success and divine presence.

verses.tsw_comparator: And David had success in all his ways, and the LORD was with him.

verses.rationale: Keeps the intensified fear as Saul’s response.

verses.tsw_comparator: And when Saul saw that he had great success, he stood in fearful awe of him.

verses.rationale: Repeats the leadership image and public love against Saul’s fear.

verses.after: But all Israel and Judah loved David, because he led them out and brought them back.

verses.rationale: Distinguishes public offer from Saul’s private plan, retaining divine-battle rhetoric.

verses.rationale: Uses kinship reading of the difficult life/family phrase, flagged in a note.

verses.rationale: Preserves passive transfer and identifies the actual husband.

verses.after: But when the time came to give Saul’s daughter Merab to David, she was given as wife to Adriel of Meholah.

verses.rationale: Keeps Michal as the subject of love rather than reducing her to Saul’s scheme.

verses.tsw_comparator: Now Michal, Saul’s daughter, loved David, and they told Saul, and the thing was pleasing in his eyes.

verses.rationale: Keeps snare and hand imagery; second-chance rendering of the difficult in-two phrase is noted.

verses.after: “I will give her to him,” Saul thought. “She can be a snare for him, so the Philistines’ hand will strike him.” He told David, “Now you have a second chance to become my son-in-law.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Saul thought, “Let me give her to him, that she may be a snare for him and that the hand of the Philistines may be against him.” Therefore Saul said to David a second time, “You shall now be my son-in-law.”

verses.rationale: Makes the instructed private persuasion and embedded speech clear.

verses.after: Saul ordered his servants, “Speak to David privately. Say, ‘The king delights in you, and all his servants love you. Become the king’s son-in-law now.’”
verses.tsw_comparator: And Saul commanded his servants, “Speak to David in private and say, ‘Behold, the king delights in you, and all his servants love you; now then become the king’s son-in-law.’”

verses.rationale: Preserves the contrast between royal marriage and David’s means and status.

verses.after: When Saul’s servants repeated this to David, he said, “Do you think becoming the king’s son-in-law is a small thing? I am poor and of little standing.”
verses.tsw_comparator: And Saul’s servants spoke those words in the ears of David. And David said, “Does it seem to you a light thing to become the king’s son-in-law, since I am a poor man and of no reputation?”

verses.rationale: Keeps the reporting step without invented dialogue.

verses.tsw_comparator: And the servants of Saul told him, “Thus and so did David speak.”

verses.rationale: Retains the bodily demand and the narrator’s exposure of Saul’s intent.

verses.rationale: Keeps both grounds for Saul’s recognition.

verses.after: Saul saw and knew that the LORD was with David and that his daughter Michal loved him.
verses.tsw_comparator: But when Saul saw and knew that the LORD was with David, and that Michal, Saul’s daughter, loved him,

verses.rationale: Preserves the escalation and enduring enmity.
verses.before: Saul was still more afraid of David. So Saul was David’s enemy continually.
verses.after: He became still more afraid of David and remained his enemy for the rest of his days.
verses.tsw_comparator: Saul was still more afraid of David. So Saul was David’s enemy continually.

verses.rationale: Keeps repeated campaigning, comparative success and name/standing.

verses.after: Whenever the Philistine commanders went out to battle, David succeeded more than all Saul’s other servants. His name became highly honored.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the commanders of the Philistines came out to battle, and as often as they came out David had more success than all the servants of Saul, so that his name was highly esteemed.

verses.rationale: Preserves the open killing order and Jonathan’s contrasting attachment.
verses.before: Saul spoke to Jonathan his son and to all his servants about putting David to death. But Jonathan son of Saul delighted greatly in David.
verses.after: Saul told his son Jonathan and all his servants to kill David. But Jonathan delighted greatly in David,
verses.tsw_comparator: Saul spoke to Jonathan his son and to all his servants about putting David to death. But Jonathan son of Saul delighted greatly in David.

verses.rationale: Makes the warning’s speaker and intended hiding time clear.

verses.rationale: Keeps the field rendezvous and promise to report without invented signals.

verses.after: I will go out and stand beside my father in the field where you are. I will speak to him about you, find out what I can, and let you know.”
verses.tsw_comparator: I will go out and stand beside my father in the field where you are, and I will speak with my father concerning you. If I see anything, I will tell you.”

verses.rationale: Retains repeated sin language and Jonathan’s respectful third-person address.

verses.after: Jonathan spoke well of David to his father Saul: “The king must not sin against his servant David. David has not sinned against you; what he has done has helped you greatly.
verses.tsw_comparator: Jonathan spoke good concerning David to Saul his father and said to him, “Let not the king sin against his servant David, because he has not sinned against you and because his deeds have been very good toward you.

verses.rationale: Preserves life-in-hand and innocent-blood images with the challenge to unjust killing.

verses.rationale: Keeps hearing the voice and the oath that later conduct contradicts.

verses.after: Saul listened to Jonathan’s voice and swore, “As the LORD lives, David will not be put to death.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Saul listened to the voice of Jonathan, and Saul swore, “As the LORD lives, he shall not be put to death.”

verses.rationale: Clarifies restored court service without asserting permanent safety.

verses.tsw_comparator: Jonathan called David, and Jonathan told him all these words. Jonathan brought David to Saul, and he was before him as formerly.

verses.rationale: Preserves the troubling divine attribution and simultaneous actions.

verses.rationale: Makes the unsuccessful attack and actual point of impact explicit.

verses.rationale: Preserves Michal’s active warning and the contrasting night/morning timing.

verses.tsw_comparator: Saul sent the messengers to see David, saying, “Bring him up to me in the bed, so that I may put him to death.”

verses.after: They set out for Ziph ahead of Saul. David and his men were in the wilderness of Maon, in the Arabah south of Jeshimon.
verses.tsw_comparator: They arose and went to Ziph before Saul. But David and his men were in the wilderness of Maon, in the Arabah south of Jeshimon.

verses.rationale: Keeps the movements and successive reports clear.
verses.before: Saul and his men went to seek him, and it was told to David. So he went down to the rock and remained in the wilderness of Maon. Saul heard and pursued David in the wilderness of Maon.
verses.after: Saul and his men went to search. When David was told, he went down to the rock and stayed in the wilderness of Maon. Saul heard and pursued him there.
verses.tsw_comparator: Saul and his men went to seek him, and it was told to David. So he went down to the rock and remained in the wilderness of Maon. Saul heard and pursued David in the wilderness of Maon.

verses.rationale: Preserves opposite sides and imminent encirclement.
verses.before: Saul went on one side of the mountain, and David and his men on the other side of the mountain. David was hurrying to get away from Saul, while Saul and his men were surrounding David and his men to seize them.
verses.after: Saul went along one side of the mountain, David and his men along the other. David hurried to get away, while Saul and his men were closing around them to seize them.
verses.tsw_comparator: Saul went on one side of the mountain, and David and his men on the other side of the mountain. David was hurrying to get away from Saul, while Saul and his men were surrounding David and his men to seize them.

verses.rationale: Retains abrupt interruption and urgent summons.
verses.before: But a messenger came to Saul, saying, “Hurry and go, for the Philistines have made a raid upon the land.”
verses.after: Then a messenger came to Saul: “Hurry and come! The Philistines have raided the land.”
verses.tsw_comparator: But a messenger came to Saul, saying, “Hurry and go, for the Philistines have made a raid upon the land.”

verses.rationale: Preserves the name explanation without choosing an unmarked etymology.
verses.before: So Saul returned from pursuing David and went to meet the Philistines. Therefore they called that place the Rock of Escape.
verses.after: Saul broke off his pursuit of David and went to meet the Philistines. That is why the place was called Sela-hammahlekoth.
verses.tsw_comparator: So Saul returned from pursuing David and went to meet the Philistines. Therefore they called that place the Rock of Escape.

verses.rationale: Binds whole Hebrew 24:1 to public 23:29 and retains ascent and refuge.
verses.before: David went up from there and stayed in the strongholds of En-Gedi.
verses.after: David went up from there and stayed in the strongholds of En-gedi.
verses.tsw_comparator: David went up from there and stayed in the strongholds of En-Gedi.

verses.rationale: Maps Hebrew 24:2 to public 24:1 and retains the renewed report.
verses.before: And it happened when Saul returned from following the Philistines that it was told to him, saying, “Look, David is in the wilderness of En-Gedi.”
verses.after: After Saul returned from pursuing the Philistines, he was told, “David is in the wilderness of En-gedi.”
verses.tsw_comparator: And it happened when Saul returned from following the Philistines that it was told to him, saying, “Look, David is in the wilderness of En-Gedi.”

verses.rationale: Keeps exact force size and named terrain.
verses.before: Saul took three thousand chosen men from all Israel and went to seek David and his men upon the Rocks of the Wild Goats.
verses.after: Saul took three thousand chosen men from all Israel and went to search for David and his men near the Rocks of the Wild Goats.
verses.tsw_comparator: Saul took three thousand chosen men from all Israel and went to seek David and his men upon the Rocks of the Wild Goats.

verses.rationale: Renders covering-feet euphemism and preserves the concealed men’s location.
verses.before: He came to the sheepfolds by the way, and there was a cave there. Saul went in to cover his feet. Now David and his men were sitting in the innermost parts of the cave.
verses.after: He came to sheepfolds beside the road, where there was a cave, and went in to relieve himself. David and his men were sitting deep inside the cave.
verses.tsw_comparator: He came to the sheepfolds by the way, and there was a cave there. Saul went in to cover his feet. Now David and his men were sitting in the innermost parts of the cave.

verses.rationale: Keeps the alleged divine promise as the men’s quotation, not a narrator endorsement.
verses.before: The men of David said to him, “Look, this is the day of which the LORD said to you, ‘Look, I am giving your enemy into your hand, and you will do to him as is good in your eyes.’” Then David arose and secretly cut off the edge of Saul’s robe.
verses.after: David’s men told him, “This is the day the LORD spoke of: ‘I am giving your enemy into your hand. Do whatever seems good to you.’” David got up and quietly cut off the edge of Saul’s robe.
verses.tsw_comparator: The men of David said to him, “Look, this is the day of which the LORD said to you, ‘Look, I am giving your enemy into your hand, and you shall do to him as is good in your eyes.’” Then David arose and secretly cut off the edge of Saul’s robe.

verses.rationale: Preserves heart striking as the source’s image of remorse.
verses.before: And it happened afterward that David’s heart struck him because he had cut off Saul’s edge.
verses.after: Afterward David’s heart struck him because he had cut off the edge of Saul’s robe.
verses.tsw_comparator: And it happened afterward that David’s heart struck him because he had cut off Saul’s edge.

verses.rationale: Retains repeated anointed and hand language central to David’s restraint.
verses.before: He said to his men, “Far be it from me by the LORD that I should do this thing to my lord, the LORD’s anointed, to stretch out my hand against him, for he is the LORD’s anointed.”
verses.after: He told his men, “The LORD forbid that I should do such a thing to my lord, the LORD’s anointed, by raising my hand against him. He is the LORD’s anointed.”
verses.tsw_comparator: He said to his men, “Far be it from me by the LORD that I should do this thing to my lord, the LORD’s anointed, to stretch out my hand against him, for he is the LORD’s anointed.”

verses.rationale: Keeps force of rebuke without rendering it as physical dismemberment.
verses.before: David restrained his men with these words and did not allow them to rise against Saul. Saul arose from the cave and went on the way.
verses.after: With these words David sharply restrained his men and would not let them attack Saul. Saul left the cave and continued on his way.
verses.tsw_comparator: David restrained his men with these words and did not allow them to rise against Saul. Saul arose from the cave and went on the way.

verses.rationale: Preserves exit, address, turn and obeisance in sequence.
verses.before: Afterward David also arose and went out from the cave and called after Saul, saying, “My lord the king!” Saul looked behind him, and David bowed with his face to the ground and prostrated himself.
verses.after: Then David came out of the cave and called after Saul, “My lord the king!” Saul looked behind him, and David bowed facedown to the ground.
verses.tsw_comparator: Afterward David also arose and went out from the cave and called after Saul, saying, “My lord the king!” Saul looked behind him, and David bowed with his face to the ground and prostrated himself.

verses.rationale: Keeps the accusation as a quoted report.
verses.before: David said to Saul, “Why do you listen to human words, saying, ‘Look, David seeks your harm’?
verses.after: David said, “Why do you listen to people who say, ‘David seeks your harm’?
verses.tsw_comparator: David said to Saul, “Why do you listen to human words, saying, ‘Look, David seeks your harm’?

verses.rationale: Takes the difficult unnamed urging and sparing clauses contextually; note preserves uncertainty.
verses.before: Look, this day your eyes have seen how the LORD gave you today into my hand in the cave. Some said to kill you, but I spared you. I said, ‘I will not stretch out my hand against my lord, for he is the LORD’s anointed.’
verses.after: Today your own eyes have seen how the LORD gave you into my hand in the cave. I was urged to kill you, but I spared you. I said, ‘I will not raise my hand against my lord, for he is the LORD’s anointed.’
verses.tsw_comparator: Look, this day your eyes have seen how the LORD gave you today into my hand in the cave. Some said to kill you, but I spared you. I said, ‘I will not stretch out my hand against my lord, for he is the LORD’s anointed.’

verses.rationale: Retains father address, evidentiary hand and life-hunting language.
verses.before: See, my father, see the edge of your robe in my hand. For in cutting off the edge of your robe and not killing you, know and see that there is no evil or rebellion in my hand. I have not sinned against you, though you hunt my life to take it.
verses.after: Look, my father! See the edge of your robe in my hand. I cut it off but did not kill you. Know and see that my hand holds no evil or rebellion. I have not sinned against you, yet you hunt my life to take it.
verses.tsw_comparator: See, my father, see the edge of your robe in my hand. For in cutting off the edge of your robe and not killing you, know and see that there is no evil or rebellion in my hand. I have not sinned against you, though you hunt my life to take it.

verses.rationale: Keeps divine vengeance beside personal restraint without recasting it as blanket pacifism.
verses.before: May the LORD judge between me and you, and may the LORD avenge me from you, but my hand will not be against you.
verses.after: May the LORD judge between us and avenge me on you. But my hand will not be against you.
verses.tsw_comparator: May the LORD judge between me and you, and may the LORD avenge me from you, but my hand shall not be against you.

verses.rationale: Preserves proverb and exact repeated refrain.
verses.before: As the proverb of the ancients says, ‘From the wicked comes wickedness,’ but my hand will not be against you.
verses.after: As the old proverb says, ‘Wickedness comes from the wicked.’ My hand will not be against you.
verses.tsw_comparator: As the proverb of the ancients says, ‘From the wicked comes wickedness,’ but my hand shall not be against you.

verses.rationale: Keeps the belittling self-images and rhetorical questions.
verses.before: After whom has the king of Israel come out? After whom are you pursuing? After a dead dog? After one flea?
verses.after: Whom has Israel’s king come out against? Whom are you pursuing? A dead dog! A single flea!
verses.tsw_comparator: After whom has the king of Israel come out? After whom are you pursuing? After a dead dog? After one flea?

verses.rationale: Preserves the judicial cluster and hand image.
verses.before: May the LORD be judge and judge between me and you. May he see and plead my cause and judge me from your hand.”
verses.after: May the LORD be judge and decide between us. May he see, plead my case, and vindicate me against your hand.”
verses.tsw_comparator: May the LORD be judge and judge between me and you. May he see and plead my cause and judge me from your hand.”

verses.rationale: Keeps voice recognition and the son address after David’s father address.
verses.before: And it happened when David finished speaking these words to Saul that Saul said, “Is this your voice, my son David?” Then Saul lifted his voice and wept.
verses.after: When David finished speaking, Saul asked, “Is that your voice, my son David?” Then Saul wept aloud.
verses.tsw_comparator: And it happened when David finished speaking these words to Saul that Saul said, “Is this your voice, my son David?” Then Saul lifted his voice and wept.

verses.rationale: Retains righteousness and matched repayment language.
verses.before: He said to David, “You are more righteous than I, for you have repaid me good while I have repaid you evil.
verses.after: He said to David, “You are more righteous than I am. You have repaid me with good, while I have repaid you with harm.
verses.tsw_comparator: He said to David, “You are more righteous than I, for you have repaid me good while I have repaid you evil.

verses.rationale: Keeps Saul’s acknowledgment of the spared opportunity.
verses.before: You have declared today how you have done good with me, how the LORD delivered me into your hand and you did not kill me.
verses.after: Today you have shown the good you have done me: the LORD handed me over to you, but you did not kill me.
verses.tsw_comparator: You have declared today how you have done good with me, how the LORD delivered me into your hand and you did not kill me.

verses.rationale: Preserves the question and good-for-good wish.
verses.before: For if a man finds his enemy, will he send him away on a good road? May the LORD repay you with good for what you have done to me this day.
verses.after: Who finds an enemy and lets him go safely? May the LORD repay you with good for what you have done for me today.
verses.tsw_comparator: For if a man finds his enemy, will he send him away on a good road? May the LORD repay you with good for what you have done to me this day.

verses.rationale: Keeps emphatic kingship and hand imagery.
verses.before: And now, look, I know that you will surely become king and that the kingdom of Israel will be established in your hand.
verses.after: Now I know that you will surely be king and that Israel’s kingdom will be established in your hand.
verses.tsw_comparator: And now, look, I know that you will surely become king and that the kingdom of Israel will be established in your hand.

verses.rationale: Preserves distinct offspring and family-name requests.
verses.before: And now swear to me by the LORD that you will not cut off my offspring after me and that you will not destroy my name from my father’s house.”
verses.after: Swear to me by the LORD that you will not cut off my offspring after me or wipe out my name from my father’s house.”
verses.tsw_comparator: And now swear to me by the LORD that you will not cut off my offspring after me and that you will not destroy my name from my father’s house.”

verses.rationale: Keeps the oath without implying David returned to Saul’s custody.
verses.before: David swore to Saul. Then Saul went to his house, but David and his men went up to the stronghold.
verses.after: David swore to Saul. Saul went home, but David and his men went up to the stronghold.
verses.tsw_comparator: David swore to Saul. Then Saul went to his house, but David and his men went up to the stronghold.

verses.rationale: Retains Samuel’s death and the pinned Paran reading without harmonizing geography.
verses.before: Samuel died, and all Israel gathered and mourned for him, and they buried him at his house in Ramah. Then David arose and went down to the wilderness of Paran.
verses.after: Samuel died. All Israel gathered to mourn him, and they buried him at his home in Ramah. David then left and went down to the wilderness of Paran.
verses.tsw_comparator: Samuel died, and all Israel gathered and mourned for him, and they buried him at his house in Ramah. Then David arose and went down to the wilderness of Paran.

verses.rationale: Keeps distinct residence/business locations and exact flock sizes.
verses.before: There was a man in Maon whose work was in Carmel. The man was very great and had three thousand sheep and one thousand goats. He was shearing his sheep in Carmel.
verses.after: A man in Maon had his business at Carmel. He was very wealthy, owning three thousand sheep and a thousand goats, and he was shearing his sheep at Carmel.
verses.tsw_comparator: There was a man in Maon whose work was in Carmel. The man was very great and had three thousand sheep and one thousand goats. He was shearing his sheep in Carmel.

verses.rationale: Preserves contrasting descriptions and qere Calebite rather than ketiv heart expression.
verses.before: The name of the man was Nabal, and the name of his wife Abigail. The woman was good in understanding and beautiful in appearance, but the man was harsh and evil in his deeds. He was a Calebite.
verses.after: His name was Nabal, and his wife’s name was Abigail. She had good judgment and was beautiful; he was harsh and acted wickedly. He was a Calebite.
verses.tsw_comparator: The name of the man was Nabal, and the name of his wife Abigail. The woman was good in understanding and beautiful in appearance, but the man was harsh and evil in his deeds. He was a Calebite.

verses.rationale: Retains the report that initiates the request.
verses.before: David heard in the wilderness that Nabal was shearing his sheep.
verses.after: In the wilderness David heard that Nabal was shearing his sheep.
verses.tsw_comparator: David heard in the wilderness that Nabal was shearing his sheep.

verses.rationale: Keeps ten emissaries and David’s authorization.
verses.before: So David sent ten young men. David said to the young men, “Go up to Carmel, come to Nabal, and ask him in my name about his well-being.
verses.after: He sent ten young men with these instructions: “Go up to Carmel and greet Nabal in my name.
verses.tsw_comparator: So David sent ten young men. David said to the young men, “Go up to Carmel, come to Nabal, and ask him in my name about his well-being.

verses.rationale: Preserves threefold peace and the difficult opening wish.
verses.before: Thus you will say: ‘Long life to you, and peace to you, peace to your house, and peace to all that belongs to you.
verses.after: Say, ‘Long life to you! Peace to you, peace to your house, and peace to all that is yours.
verses.tsw_comparator: Thus you shall say: ‘Long life to you, and peace to you, peace to your house, and peace to all that belongs to you.

verses.rationale: Retains the two distinct claims of conduct and protection.
verses.before: And now I have heard that you have shearers. Your shepherds were with us; we did not humiliate them, and nothing of theirs was missing all the days they were in Carmel.
verses.after: I hear that you have shearers at work. Your shepherds have been with us. We did not mistreat them, and nothing of theirs went missing all the time they were at Carmel.
verses.tsw_comparator: And now I have heard that you have shearers. Your shepherds were with us; we did not humiliate them, and nothing of theirs was missing all the days they were in Carmel.

verses.rationale: Keeps request, festive timing and deferential son/servant language.
verses.before: Ask your young men, and they will tell you. Therefore let the young men find favor in your eyes, for we have come on a good day. Please give whatever your hand finds to your servants and to your son David.’”
verses.after: Ask your young men; they will tell you. May these young men find favor with you, for we have come on a festive day. Please give whatever you can to your servants and to your son David.’”
verses.tsw_comparator: Ask your young men, and they will tell you. Therefore let the young men find favor in your eyes, for we have come on a good day. Please give whatever your hand finds to your servants and to your son David.’”

verses.rationale: Renders rested as waiting after the speech while retaining sequence.
verses.before: David’s young men came and spoke to Nabal according to all these words in David’s name. Then they waited.
verses.after: David’s young men came and spoke all these words to Nabal in David’s name. Then they waited.
verses.tsw_comparator: David’s young men came and spoke to Nabal according to all these words in David’s name. Then they waited.

verses.rationale: Keeps the contemptuous questions and comparison with runaway servants.
verses.before: Nabal answered David’s servants and said, “Who is David? And who is the son of Jesse? Many servants today are breaking away, each from his master.
verses.after: Nabal answered David’s servants, “Who is David? Who is Jesse’s son? There are plenty of servants breaking away from their masters these days.
verses.tsw_comparator: Nabal answered David’s servants and said, “Who is David? And who is the son of Jesse? Many servants today are breaking away, each from his master.

verses.rationale: Preserves possessive repetition and the pinned water rather than wine.
verses.before: Will I take my bread, my water, and my meat that I slaughtered for my shearers and give it to men whose origin I do not know?”
verses.after: Should I take my bread, my water, and the meat I slaughtered for my shearers and give it to men when I do not even know where they come from?”
verses.tsw_comparator: Shall I take my bread, my water, and my meat that I slaughtered for my shearers and give it to men whose origin I do not know?”

verses.rationale: Keeps the full report after failed request.
verses.before: David’s young men turned on their way, returned, and came and told him according to all these words.
verses.after: David’s young men turned back, returned to him, and reported everything Nabal had said.
verses.tsw_comparator: David’s young men turned on their way, returned, and came and told him according to all these words.

verses.rationale: Preserves repeated arming and the split of six hundred men.
verses.before: David said to his men, “Each man strap on his sword.” So each man strapped on his sword, and David also strapped on his sword. About four hundred men went up after David, while two hundred remained with the baggage.
verses.after: David told his men, “Strap on your swords!” Every man did so, and David strapped on his own. About four hundred followed him, while two hundred stayed with the supplies.
verses.tsw_comparator: David said to his men, “Each man strap on his sword.” So each man strapped on his sword, and David also strapped on his sword. About four hundred men went up after David, while two hundred remained with the baggage.

verses.rationale: Keeps servant’s initiative and his account of the insult.
verses.before: But one young man from the young men told Abigail, Nabal’s wife, saying, “Look, David sent messengers from the wilderness to bless our master, but he screamed insults at them.
verses.after: One of the servants told Abigail, Nabal’s wife, “David sent messengers from the wilderness to bless our master, but he railed at them.
verses.tsw_comparator: But one young man from the young men told Abigail, Nabal’s wife, saying, “Look, David sent messengers from the wilderness to bless our master, but he screamed insults at them.

verses.rationale: Preserves independent confirmation of David’s protective conduct.
verses.before: Yet the men were very good to us. We were not humiliated, and we did not miss anything all the days we went about with them while we were in the field.
verses.after: Those men were very good to us. They did not mistreat us, and nothing went missing while we were out in the fields with them.
verses.tsw_comparator: Yet the men were very good to us. We were not humiliated, and we did not miss anything all the days we went about with them while we were in the field.

verses.rationale: Retains wall image and uninterrupted protection.
verses.before: They were a wall around us both night and day all the days we were with them shepherding the flock.
verses.after: They were a wall around us, night and day, the whole time we were with them tending the flock.
verses.tsw_comparator: They were a wall around us both night and day all the days we were with them shepherding the flock.

verses.rationale: Keeps household danger and the servant’s harsh judgment as speech.
verses.before: And now know and see what you should do, for evil is determined against our master and against all his house. He is such a worthless man that no one can speak to him.”
verses.after: Now consider what you should do. Harm is determined against our master and his whole household. He is such a worthless man that no one can speak to him.”
verses.tsw_comparator: And now know and see what you should do, for evil is determined against our master and against all his house. He is such a worthless man that no one can speak to him.”

verses.rationale: Preserves every food item and quantity, following qere prepared.
verses.before: Abigail hurried and took two hundred loaves, two skins of wine, five sheep prepared for food, five seahs of roasted grain, one hundred clusters of raisins, and two hundred cakes of figs, and put them upon donkeys.
verses.after: Abigail hurried. She took two hundred loaves, two skins of wine, five prepared sheep, five seahs of roasted grain, a hundred raisin cakes, and two hundred fig cakes, and loaded them on donkeys.
verses.tsw_comparator: Abigail hurried and took two hundred loaves, two skins of wine, five sheep prepared for food, five seahs of roasted grain, one hundred clusters of raisins, and two hundred cakes of figs, and put them upon donkeys.

verses.rationale: Keeps Abigail’s independent action and deliberate nondisclosure.
verses.before: She said to her young men, “Pass on before me. Look, I am coming after you.” But she did not tell Nabal her husband.
verses.after: “Go ahead of me,” she told her servants. “I will follow you.” She did not tell her husband Nabal.
verses.tsw_comparator: She said to her young men, “Pass on before me. Look, I am coming after you.” But she did not tell Nabal her husband.

verses.rationale: Preserves obscured approach and encounter without inventing topography.
verses.before: And it happened as she was riding on the donkey and going down by the hidden part of the mountain, look, David and his men were coming down toward her, and she met them.
verses.after: She rode her donkey down a hidden slope of the mountain. David and his men were coming down toward her, and she met them.
verses.tsw_comparator: And it happened as she was riding on the donkey and going down by the hidden part of the mountain, behold, David and his men were coming down toward her, and she met them.

verses.rationale: Keeps the earlier statement and repeated repayment contrast from chapter 24.
verses.before: Now David had said, “Surely for emptiness I guarded all that belongs to this man in the wilderness, so that nothing was missing from all that belonged to him, and he returned evil to me for good.
verses.after: David had said, “It was all for nothing that I guarded this man’s possessions in the wilderness so that none went missing. He has repaid me harm for good.
verses.tsw_comparator: Now David had said, “Surely for emptiness I guarded all that belongs to this man in the wilderness, so that nothing was missing from all that belonged to him, and he returned evil to me for good.

verses.rationale: Preserves the pinned enemies in the oath and the coarse male designation; both noted.
verses.before: Thus may God do to David’s enemies and more also if I leave by morning from everyone who belong to him one who urinates against a wall.”
verses.after: May God do this to David’s enemies, and more, if by morning I leave him a single one who urinates against a wall!”
verses.tsw_comparator: Thus may God do to David’s enemies and more also if I leave by morning from all who belong to him one who urinates against a wall.”

verses.rationale: Retains her urgency and bodily posture.
verses.before: When Abigail saw David, she hurried and got down from the donkey, fell before David upon her face, and bowed down to the ground.
verses.after: When Abigail saw David, she hurried off the donkey and fell facedown before him, bowing to the ground.
verses.tsw_comparator: When Abigail saw David, she hurried and got down from the donkey, fell before David upon her face, and bowed down to the ground.

verses.rationale: Keeps her assumption of blame as strategic speech rather than narrator judgment.
verses.before: She fell at his feet and said, “Upon me, my lord, be the guilt. Please let your female servant speak in your ears, and hear the words of your female servant.
verses.after: She fell at his feet and said, “Let the guilt be mine, my lord. Please let your servant speak, and listen to her words.
verses.tsw_comparator: She fell at his feet and said, “Upon me, my lord, be the guilt. Please let your female servant speak in your ears, and hear the words of your female servant.

verses.rationale: Preserves name/folly wordplay and Abigail’s absence from the initial encounter.
verses.before: Please let not my lord set his heart toward this worthless man, toward Nabal, for as his name is, so is he. Nabal is his name, and folly is with him. But I, your female servant, did not see the young men of my lord whom you sent.
verses.after: My lord, pay no attention to this worthless man Nabal. He is just what his name says: his name is Nabal, and folly goes with him. But I, your servant, did not see the young men you sent.
verses.tsw_comparator: Please let not my lord set his heart toward this worthless man, toward Nabal, for as his name is, so is he. Nabal is his name, and folly is with him. But I, your female servant, did not see the young men of my lord whom you sent.

verses.rationale: Retains her anticipatory claim of restraint and hand-deliverance image.
verses.before: And now, my lord, as the LORD lives and as your life lives, since the LORD has restrained you from coming into bloodguilt and from saving yourself with your own hand, now let your enemies and those seeking evil against my lord be like Nabal.
verses.after: Now, my lord, as the LORD lives and as you live, the LORD has kept you from bloodguilt and from winning deliverance by your own hand. May your enemies and those who seek your harm be like Nabal.
verses.tsw_comparator: And now, my lord, as the LORD lives and as your life lives, since the LORD has restrained you from coming into bloodguilt and from saving yourself with your own hand, now let your enemies and those seeking evil against my lord be like Nabal.

verses.rationale: Keeps gift as blessing and directs it to the accompanying men.
verses.before: And now, let this blessing that your female servant has brought to my lord be given to the young men who walk at the feet of my lord.
verses.after: Let this blessing your servant has brought my lord be given to the young men who follow you.
verses.tsw_comparator: And now, let this blessing that your female servant has brought to my lord be given to the young men who walk at the feet of my lord.

verses.rationale: Preserves lasting-house promise and treats the final clause as a wish, noted as uncertain.
verses.before: Please forgive the transgression of your female servant, for the LORD will surely make for my lord an enduring house, because my lord fights the battles of the LORD, and evil will not be found in you all your days.
verses.after: Please forgive your servant’s offense. The LORD will surely establish a lasting house for my lord, because you fight the LORD’s battles. May no evil be found in you throughout your days.
verses.tsw_comparator: Please forgive the transgression of your female servant, for the LORD will surely make for my lord an enduring house, because my lord fights the battles of the LORD, and evil shall not be found in you all your days.

verses.rationale: Keeps paired bundle and sling images rather than abstracting protection and judgment.
verses.before: Though a human being arises to pursue you and seek your life, the life of my lord will be bound in the bundle of the living with the LORD your God, but the life of your enemies he will sling away from the hollow of the sling.
verses.after: Though someone rises to pursue you and seek your life, may my lord’s life be bound in the bundle of the living with the LORD your God. But may he sling away your enemies’ lives from the pocket of a sling.
verses.tsw_comparator: Though a human being arises to pursue you and seek your life, the life of my lord shall be bound in the bundle of the living with the LORD your God, but the life of your enemies he shall sling away from the hollow of the sling.

verses.rationale: Keeps future condition running into its consequence.
verses.before: And it will be when the LORD does for my lord according to all the good that he has spoken concerning you and appoints you ruler over Israel,
verses.after: When the LORD has done for my lord all the good he has promised and appointed you leader over Israel,
verses.tsw_comparator: And it shall be when the LORD does for my lord according to all the good that he has spoken concerning you and appoints you ruler over Israel,

verses.rationale: Retains bodily conscience imagery, bloodguilt and the closing personal request.
verses.before: then this will not be for you a stumbling or a troubled heart to my lord, either that you poured out blood without cause or that my lord saved himself. And when the LORD does good to my lord, remember your female servant.”
verses.after: you will have no staggering burden or stumbling heart from shedding blood without cause or winning your own deliverance. When the LORD does good to my lord, remember your servant.”
verses.tsw_comparator: then this shall not be for you a stumbling or a troubled heart to my lord, either that you poured out blood without cause or that my lord saved himself. And when the LORD does good to my lord, remember your female servant.”

verses.rationale: Keeps David’s recognition of her arrival as divine intervention.
verses.before: David said to Abigail, “Blessed be the LORD, the God of Israel, who sent you this day to meet me.
verses.after: David answered Abigail, “Blessed be the LORD, the God of Israel, who sent you to meet me today!
verses.tsw_comparator: David said to Abigail, “Blessed be the LORD, the God of Israel, who sent you this day to meet me.

verses.rationale: Repeats her terms and explicitly credits her judgment and action.
verses.before: Blessed be your discernment, and blessed be you, who have restrained me this day from coming into bloodguilt and from saving myself with my own hand.
verses.after: Blessed be your judgment, and blessed be you! Today you kept me from bloodguilt and from winning deliverance by my own hand.
verses.tsw_comparator: Blessed be your discernment, and blessed be you, who have restrained me this day from coming into bloodguilt and from saving myself with my own hand.

verses.rationale: Preserves the repeated coarse male threat and David’s acknowledgment of intended harm.
verses.before: For truly, as the LORD, the God of Israel, lives, who restrained me from doing evil to you, unless you had hurried and come to meet me, surely by the morning light there would not have remained to Nabal one who urinates against a wall.”
verses.after: As the LORD, the God of Israel, lives, he has kept me from harming you. If you had not hurried to meet me, by dawn Nabal would not have had a single one left who urinates against a wall.”
verses.tsw_comparator: For truly, as the LORD, the God of Israel, lives, who restrained me from doing evil to you, unless you had hurried and come to meet me, surely by the morning light there would not have remained to Nabal one who urinates against a wall.”

verses.rationale: Retains hearing-voice theme and positive response to her appeal.
verses.before: Then David took from her hand what she had brought him and said to her, “Go up in peace to your house. See, I have listened to your voice and lifted up your face.”
verses.after: David accepted what she had brought and said, “Go home in peace. I have listened to your voice and granted your request.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Then David took from her hand what she had brought him and said to her, “Go up in peace to your house. See, I have listened to your voice and lifted up your face.”

verses.rationale: Keeps kinglike excess and her delayed disclosure.
verses.before: Abigail came to Nabal, and look, he had a feast in his house like the feast of a king. Nabal’s heart was merry within him, and he was very drunk. So she did not tell him anything, small or great, until the morning light.
verses.after: Abigail returned to Nabal. He was holding a banquet at home like a king’s banquet, cheerful and very drunk. She told him nothing, great or small, until morning light.
verses.tsw_comparator: Abigail came to Nabal, and behold, he had a feast in his house like the feast of a king. Nabal’s heart was merry within him, and he was very drunk. So she did not tell him anything, small or great, until the morning light.

verses.rationale: Preserves bodily imagery without diagnosing stroke or heart attack.
verses.before: And it happened in the morning, when the wine had gone out from Nabal, that his wife told him these things. His heart died within him, and he became like stone.
verses.after: In the morning, when the wine had left Nabal, his wife told him what had happened. His heart died within him, and he became like stone.
verses.tsw_comparator: And it happened in the morning, when the wine had gone out from Nabal, that his wife told him these things. His heart died within him, and he became like stone.

verses.rationale: Retains approximate interval and narrator’s divine attribution.
verses.before: And it happened about ten days later that the LORD struck Nabal, and he died.
verses.after: About ten days later, the LORD struck Nabal, and he died.
verses.tsw_comparator: And it happened about ten days later that the LORD struck Nabal, and he died.

verses.rationale: Keeps David’s interpretation within speech and subsequent marriage proposal.
verses.before: David heard that Nabal was dead and said, “Blessed be the LORD, who pleaded the case of my reproach from the hand of Nabal and restrained his servant from evil. The evil of Nabal the LORD has returned upon his own head.” Then David sent and spoke concerning Abigail, to take her for himself as wife.
verses.after: When David heard that Nabal had died, he said, “Blessed be the LORD! He has pleaded my case over Nabal’s insult and kept his servant from doing harm. The LORD has brought Nabal’s evil back on his own head.” Then David sent word to Abigail, asking to take her as his wife.
verses.tsw_comparator: David heard that Nabal was dead and said, “Blessed be the LORD, who pleaded the case of my reproach from the hand of Nabal and restrained his servant from evil. The evil of Nabal the LORD has returned upon his own head.” Then David sent and spoke concerning Abigail, to take her for himself as wife.

verses.rationale: Preserves the formal message and destination.
verses.before: David’s servants came to Abigail at Carmel and spoke to her, saying, “David has sent us to you to take you to him as wife.”
verses.after: David’s servants came to Abigail at Carmel and said, “David has sent us to take you to him as his wife.”
verses.tsw_comparator: David’s servants came to Abigail at Carmel and spoke to her, saying, “David has sent us to you to take you to him as wife.”

verses.rationale: Retains her deferential response and concrete foot-washing offer.
verses.before: She arose, bowed with her face to the ground, and said, “Look, your female servant is a servant to wash the feet of the servants of my lord.”
verses.after: She rose, bowed facedown to the ground, and said, “Here is your servant, ready to serve and wash the feet of my lord’s servants.”
verses.tsw_comparator: She arose, bowed with her face to the ground, and said, “Look, your female servant is a servant to wash the feet of the servants of my lord.”

verses.rationale: Keeps five attendants and the completed marriage.
verses.before: Abigail hurried and arose and rode on a donkey, with five of her young women walking at her feet. She went after the messengers of David and became his wife.
verses.after: Abigail quickly got ready and mounted a donkey. With five young women attending her, she followed David’s messengers and became his wife.
verses.tsw_comparator: Abigail hurried and arose and rode on a donkey, with five of her young women walking at her feet. She went after the messengers of David and became his wife.

verses.rationale: Retains plural wives and separate geographic identification.
verses.before: David had also taken Ahinoam from Jezreel, and the two of them became his wives.
