verses.after: David had also taken Ahinoam of Jezreel, and both women became his wives.
verses.tsw_comparator: David had also taken Ahinoam from Jezreel, and the two of them became his wives.

verses.rationale: Preserves Michal’s identification as David’s wife despite Saul’s transfer.
verses.before: Yet Saul had given Michal his daughter, David’s wife, to Palti son of Laish, who was from Gallim.
verses.after: Saul, meanwhile, had given his daughter Michal, David’s wife, to Palti son of Laish from Gallim.
verses.tsw_comparator: But Saul had given Michal his daughter, David’s wife, to Palti son of Laish, who was from Gallim.

verses.rationale: Keeps repeated informants and exact location.
verses.before: The Ziphites came to Saul at Gibeah, saying, “Is not David hiding on the hill of Hachilah, facing Jeshimon?”
verses.after: The Ziphites came to Saul at Gibeah and said, “David is hiding on the hill of Hachilah, facing Jeshimon.”
verses.tsw_comparator: The Ziphites came to Saul at Gibeah, saying, “Is not David hiding on the hill of Hachilah, facing Jeshimon?”

verses.rationale: Preserves the selected force and renewed pursuit.
verses.before: So Saul arose and went down to the wilderness of Ziph, and with him three thousand chosen men of Israel, to seek David in the wilderness of Ziph.
verses.after: Saul set out for the wilderness of Ziph with three thousand chosen Israelites to search for David there.
verses.tsw_comparator: So Saul arose and went down to the wilderness of Ziph, and with him three thousand chosen men of Israel, to seek David in the wilderness of Ziph.

verses.rationale: Distinguishes Saul’s camp from David’s location and awareness.
verses.before: Saul camped on the hill of Hachilah, which is facing Jeshimon, beside the road. But David was staying in the wilderness. He saw that Saul had come after him into the wilderness.
verses.after: He camped beside the road on the hill of Hachilah, facing Jeshimon. David was staying in the wilderness and saw that Saul had come after him.
verses.tsw_comparator: Saul camped on the hill of Hachilah, which is facing Jeshimon, beside the road. But David was staying in the wilderness. He saw that Saul had come after him into the wilderness.

verses.rationale: Reads the difficult certainty/location phrase as reliable intelligence, noted.
verses.before: David sent out spies and knew that Saul had surely come.
verses.after: David sent scouts and learned for certain that Saul had arrived.
verses.tsw_comparator: David sent out spies and knew that Saul had surely come.

verses.rationale: Preserves camp arrangement and both named men.
verses.before: David arose and came to the place where Saul had camped. David saw the place where Saul lay and Abner son of Ner, commander of his army. Saul was lying within the camp circle, and the people were camped around him.
verses.after: David went to Saul’s camp and saw where Saul and his army commander Abner son of Ner were lying. Saul lay inside the camp enclosure, with the troops encamped around him.
verses.tsw_comparator: David arose and came to the place where Saul had camped. David saw the place where Saul lay and Abner son of Ner, commander of his army. Saul was lying within the camp circle, and the people were camped around him.

verses.rationale: Retains the Hittite and the maternal/familial identification of Abishai.
verses.before: David answered and said to Ahimelech the Hittite and to Abishai son of Zeruiah, brother of Joab, saying, “Who will go down with me to Saul, to the camp?” Abishai said, “I will go down with you.”
verses.after: David asked Ahimelech the Hittite and Abishai son of Zeruiah, Joab’s brother, “Who will go down with me into Saul’s camp?” Abishai answered, “I will.”
verses.tsw_comparator: David answered and said to Ahimelech the Hittite and to Abishai son of Zeruiah, brother of Joab, saying, “Who will go down with me to Saul, to the camp?” Abishai said, “I will go down with you.”

verses.rationale: Keeps the spear’s exact position and sleeping protectors.
verses.before: So David and Abishai came to the people by night, and look, Saul was lying asleep within the camp circle, with his spear stuck in the ground at his head. Abner and the people were lying around him.
verses.after: David and Abishai entered the camp at night. Saul lay asleep inside the enclosure, his spear stuck in the ground beside his head. Abner and the troops lay around him.
verses.tsw_comparator: So David and Abishai came to the people by night, and behold, Saul was lying asleep within the camp circle, with his spear stuck in the ground at his head. Abner and the people were lying around him.

verses.rationale: Preserves Abishai’s claimed opportunity and violent confidence as speech.
verses.before: Abishai said to David, “God has shut your enemy into your hand this day. And now please let me strike him with the spear to the ground with one stroke, and I will not strike him a second time.”
verses.after: Abishai told David, “Today God has handed your enemy over to you. Let me pin him to the ground with one thrust of the spear. I will not need a second.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Abishai said to David, “God has shut your enemy into your hand this day. And now please let me strike him with the spear to the ground with one stroke, and I will not strike him a second time.”

verses.rationale: Retains anointed and guilt/innocence claim central to restraint.
verses.before: Yet David said to Abishai, “Do not destroy him, for who can stretch out his hand against the LORD’s anointed and be innocent?”
verses.after: David answered, “Do not destroy him. Who can raise a hand against the LORD’s anointed and remain innocent?”
verses.tsw_comparator: But David said to Abishai, “Do not destroy him, for who can stretch out his hand against the LORD’s anointed and be innocent?”

verses.rationale: Keeps the three possible ends distinct without predicting which occurs.
verses.before: David said, “As the LORD lives, surely the LORD will strike him, or his day will come and he will die, or he will go down into battle and be swept away.
verses.after: He added, “As the LORD lives, the LORD will strike him, or his day will come and he will die, or he will go down to battle and perish.
verses.tsw_comparator: David said, “As the LORD lives, surely the LORD will strike him, or his day will come and he will die, or he will go down into battle and be swept away.

verses.rationale: Preserves refusal and the two objects to be taken.
verses.before: Far be it from me by the LORD that I should stretch out my hand against the LORD’s anointed. And now, please take the spear that is at his head and the jar of water, and let us go.”
verses.after: The LORD forbid that I should raise my hand against the LORD’s anointed. Take the spear beside his head and the water flask, and let us go.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Far be it from me by the LORD that I should stretch out my hand against the LORD’s anointed. And now, please take the spear that is at his head and the jar of water, and let us go.”

verses.rationale: Retains triple no-one and the narrator’s explanation of divine sleep.
verses.before: So David took the spear and the jar of water from Saul’s head, and they went away. No one saw, no one knew, and no one awakened, for all of them were sleeping because a deep sleep from the LORD had fallen upon them.
verses.after: David took the spear and the water flask from beside Saul’s head, and they left. No one saw, no one knew, and no one woke. They were all asleep, for a deep sleep from the LORD had fallen on them.
verses.tsw_comparator: So David took the spear and the jar of water from Saul’s head, and they went away. No one saw, no one knew, and no one awakened, for all of them were sleeping because a deep sleep from the LORD had fallen upon them.

verses.rationale: Keeps protective distance before public challenge.
verses.before: David crossed to the other side and stood on the top of the mountain at a distance. There was much space between them.
verses.after: David crossed to the other side and stood far away on the hilltop, leaving a great distance between them.
verses.tsw_comparator: David crossed to the other side and stood on the top of the mountain at a distance. There was much space between them.

verses.rationale: Preserves the different addressees in challenge and reply.
verses.before: David called to the people and to Abner son of Ner, saying, “Will you not answer, Abner?” Abner answered and said, “Who are you who calls to the king?”
verses.after: He called to the troops and to Abner son of Ner, “Will you not answer, Abner?” Abner answered, “Who are you, calling to the king?”
verses.tsw_comparator: David called to the people and to Abner son of Ner, saying, “Will you not answer, Abner?” Abner answered and said, “Who are you who calls to the king?”

verses.rationale: Keeps taunts to Abner’s standing and failure as guardian.
verses.before: David said to Abner, “Are you not a man? And who is like you in Israel? Why then have you not guarded your lord the king? For one of the people came to destroy the king your lord.
verses.after: David said, “Are you not a man? Who is your equal in Israel? Why did you not guard your lord the king? Someone came to destroy him.
verses.tsw_comparator: David said to Abner, “Are you not a man? And who is like you in Israel? Why then have you not guarded your lord the king? For one of the people came to destroy the king your lord.

verses.rationale: Preserves shift to plural guards and physical evidence of failure.
verses.before: This thing that you have done is not good. As the LORD lives, you are sons of death because you did not guard your lord, the LORD’s anointed. And now see where the king’s spear is and the jar of water that was at his head.”
verses.after: What you have done is not good. As the LORD lives, you all deserve death, because you did not guard your lord, the LORD’s anointed. Now look: where are the king’s spear and the water flask that were beside his head?”
verses.tsw_comparator: This thing that you have done is not good. As the LORD lives, you are sons of death because you did not guard your lord, the LORD’s anointed. And now see where the king’s spear is and the jar of water that was at his head.”

verses.rationale: Repeats the earlier recognition wording and respectful reply.
verses.before: Saul recognized David’s voice and said, “Is this your voice, my son David?” David said, “It is my voice, my lord the king.”
verses.after: Saul recognized David’s voice. “Is that your voice, my son David?” he asked. David answered, “It is my voice, my lord the king.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Saul recognized David’s voice and said, “Is this your voice, my son David?” David said, “It is my voice, my lord the king.”

verses.rationale: Preserves respectful third-person speech and hand image of conduct.
verses.before: He said, “Why does my lord pursue after his servant? For what have I done? And what evil is in my hand?
verses.after: He said, “Why is my lord pursuing his servant? What have I done? What evil is in my hand?
verses.tsw_comparator: He said, “Why does my lord pursue after his servant? For what have I done? And what evil is in my hand?

verses.rationale: Retains the difficult divine-incitement possibility, offering scent and forced religious displacement.
verses.before: And now, please let my lord the king hear the words of his servant. If the LORD has incited you against me, let him smell an offering. But if it is human beings, cursed are they before the LORD, for they have driven me out this day from sharing in the inheritance of the LORD, saying, ‘Go, serve other gods.’
verses.after: My lord the king, please listen to your servant’s words. If the LORD has stirred you up against me, may he accept the scent of an offering. But if people have done it, may they be cursed before the LORD. Today they have driven me from my share in the LORD’s inheritance, saying, ‘Go and serve other gods.’
verses.tsw_comparator: And now, please let my lord the king hear the words of his servant. If the LORD has incited you against me, let him smell an offering. But if it is human beings, cursed are they before the LORD, for they have driven me out this day from sharing in the inheritance of the LORD, saying, ‘Go, serve other gods.’

verses.rationale: Keeps blood, presence, flea and hunted-bird images without reconciling their scale.
verses.before: And now, do not let my blood fall to the ground away from the presence of the LORD, for the king of Israel has come out to seek one flea, as one hunts a partridge in the mountains.”
verses.after: Do not let my blood fall to the ground far from the LORD’s presence. Israel’s king has come out to seek a single flea, as one hunts a partridge in the mountains.”
verses.tsw_comparator: And now, do not let my blood fall to the ground away from the presence of the LORD, for the king of Israel has come out to seek one flea, as one hunts a partridge in the mountains.”

verses.rationale: Preserves confession, appeal and recognition of spared life.
verses.before: Saul said, “I have sinned. Return, my son David, for I will no longer do you harm because my life was precious in your eyes this day. Look, I have acted foolishly and have erred exceedingly.”
verses.after: Saul said, “I have sinned. Come back, my son David. I will not harm you again, because you valued my life today. I have acted foolishly and gone very far astray.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Saul said, “I have sinned. Return, my son David, for I will no longer do you harm because my life was precious in your eyes this day. Look, I have acted foolishly and have erred exceedingly.”

verses.rationale: Keeps David apart from Saul while returning the spear.
verses.before: David answered and said, “Look, the king’s spear. Let one of the young men cross over and take it.
verses.after: David answered, “Here is the king’s spear. Let one of the young men come over and get it.
verses.tsw_comparator: David answered and said, “Look, the king’s spear. Let one of the young men cross over and take it.

verses.rationale: Retains repayment, righteousness/faithfulness and repeated hand language.
verses.before: The LORD will return to each man his righteousness and his faithfulness, for the LORD gave you into my hand today, but I was not willing to stretch out my hand against the LORD’s anointed.
verses.after: The LORD repays each person’s righteousness and faithfulness. Today he gave you into my hand, but I would not raise my hand against the LORD’s anointed.
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD will return to each man his righteousness and his faithfulness, for the LORD gave you into my hand today, but I was not willing to stretch out my hand against the LORD’s anointed.

verses.rationale: Preserves the comparison while directing hope to the LORD rather than Saul.
verses.before: And look, as your life was great in my eyes this day, so may my life be great in the eyes of the LORD, and may he rescue me from every distress.”
verses.after: As I valued your life today, may the LORD value mine and rescue me from every distress.”
verses.tsw_comparator: And look, as your life was great in my eyes this day, so may my life be great in the eyes of the LORD, and may he rescue me from every distress.”

verses.rationale: Keeps blessing and separate departures without inventing reconciliation.
verses.before: Saul said to David, “Blessed are you, my son David. You will surely do and surely prevail.” Then David went on his way, and Saul returned to his place.
verses.after: Saul told David, “Blessed are you, my son David. You will do great things and surely prevail.” David went his own way, and Saul returned to his place.
verses.tsw_comparator: Saul said to David, “Blessed are you, my son David. You will surely do and surely prevail.” Then David went on his way, and Saul returned to his place.

verses.rationale: Keeps inner speech, fear and repeated hand/escape without narrator endorsement of the plan.
verses.before: David said in his heart, “Now I will perish one day by the hand of Saul. There is nothing better for me than that I escape, escape to the land of the Philistines. Then Saul will despair of seeking me any more throughout all the territory of Israel, and I will escape from his hand.”
verses.after: David said to himself, “One day Saul’s hand will sweep me away. My best course is to escape to Philistine territory. Then Saul will give up searching for me throughout Israel, and I will escape his hand.”
verses.tsw_comparator: David said in his heart, “Now I will perish one day by the hand of Saul. There is nothing better for me than that I escape, escape to the land of the Philistines. Then Saul will despair of seeking me any more throughout all the territory of Israel, and I will escape from his hand.”

verses.rationale: Retains band size, patronymic and crossing.
verses.before: So David arose and crossed over, he and six hundred men who were with him, to Achish son of Maoch, king of Gath.
verses.after: David set out with his six hundred men and crossed over to Achish son of Maoch, king of Gath.
verses.tsw_comparator: So David arose and crossed over, he and six hundred men who were with him, to Achish son of Maoch, king of Gath.

verses.rationale: Preserves household migration and Abigail’s continuing identification with Nabal.
verses.before: David lived with Achish at Gath, he and his men, each man with his household, and David with his two wives, Ahinoam the Jezreelite and Abigail wife of Nabal the Carmelite.
verses.after: David and his men settled with Achish in Gath, each with his household. David had his two wives with him: Ahinoam of Jezreel and Abigail of Carmel, Nabal’s wife.
verses.tsw_comparator: David lived with Achish at Gath, he and his men, each man with his household, and David with his two wives, Ahinoam the Jezreelite and Abigail wife of Nabal the Carmelite.

verses.rationale: Keeps the effect of David’s move and qere ceased.
verses.before: It was told to Saul that David had fled to Gath, and he did not continue to seek him.
verses.after: When Saul was told that David had fled to Gath, he stopped searching for him.
verses.tsw_comparator: It was told to Saul that David had fled to Gath, and he did not continue to seek him.

verses.rationale: Retains deferential request for separate residence.
verses.before: David said to Achish, “If now I have found favor in your eyes, let them give me a place in one of the cities of the countryside, and I will live there. Why should your servant live in the royal city with you?”
verses.after: David said to Achish, “If I have found favor with you, give me a place in one of the country towns to live. Why should your servant live with you in the royal city?”
verses.tsw_comparator: David said to Achish, “If now I have found favor in your eyes, let them give me a place in one of the cities of the countryside, and I will live there. Why should your servant live in the royal city with you?”

verses.rationale: Keeps the narrator’s later-looking explanation without modernizing its date.
verses.before: So Achish gave him Ziklag on that day. Therefore Ziklag has belonged to the kings of Judah to this day.
verses.after: That day Achish gave him Ziklag. This is why Ziklag has belonged to Judah’s kings to this day.
verses.tsw_comparator: So Achish gave him Ziklag on that day. Therefore Ziklag has belonged to the kings of Judah to this day.

verses.rationale: Renders days as the annual interval in context, with exact four months retained.
verses.before: The number of days that David lived in the territory of the Philistines was a year and four months.
verses.after: David lived in Philistine territory for a year and four months.
verses.tsw_comparator: The number of days that David lived in the territory of the Philistines was a year and four months.

verses.rationale: Follows the read form Gizrites, distinct from the written Girzites; retains the other peoples and geographical extent.
verses.before: David and his men went up and raided the Geshurites, the Girzites, and the Amalekites, for those peoples had inhabited the land from ancient times as far as Shur and as far as the land of Egypt.
verses.after: David and his men went out raiding the Geshurites, the Gizrites, and the Amalekites. These peoples had long inhabited the land stretching toward Shur and the land of Egypt.
verses.tsw_comparator: David and his men went up and raided the Geshurites, the Girzites, and the Amalekites, for those peoples had inhabited the land from ancient times as far as Shur and as far as the land of Egypt.

verses.rationale: Keeps deliberate killing of all men and women and every plunder category.
verses.before: David struck the land and did not keep alive man or woman. He took sheep, cattle, donkeys, camels, and garments and returned and came to Achish.
verses.after: Whenever David struck a district, he left neither man nor woman alive. He took sheep, cattle, donkeys, camels, and clothing, then returned to Achish.
verses.tsw_comparator: David struck the land and did not keep alive man or woman. He took sheep, cattle, donkeys, camels, and garments and returned and came to Achish.

verses.rationale: Renders difficult interrogative contextually and keeps false raid reports distinct from actual targets.
verses.before: Achish would say, “Where have you raided today?” David would say, “Against the Negev of Judah,” or “against the Negev of the Jerahmeelites,” or “against the Negev of the Kenites.”
verses.after: Achish would ask, “Where did you raid today?” David would answer, “The Negeb of Judah,” or “The Negeb of the Jerahmeelites,” or “The Negeb of the Kenites.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Achish would say, “Where have you raided today?” David would say, “Against the Negev of Judah,” or “against the Negev of the Jerahmeelites,” or “against the Negev of the Kenites.”

verses.rationale: Preserves the stated silencing of witnesses and sustained practice without excusing it.
verses.before: David did not keep alive man or woman to bring to Gath, saying, “Lest they tell concerning us, saying, ‘Thus David did.’” And such was his practice all the days that he lived in the territory of the Philistines.
verses.after: David left neither man nor woman alive to bring back to Gath. “They might report on us,” he said, “‘This is what David did.’” This was his practice all the time he lived in Philistine territory.
verses.tsw_comparator: David did not keep alive man or woman to bring to Gath, saying, “Lest they tell concerning us, saying, ‘Thus David did.’” And such was his practice all the days that he lived in the territory of the Philistines.

verses.rationale: Keeps Achish’s mistaken inference and stench metaphor.
verses.before: Achish trusted David, saying, “He has surely made himself odious among his people Israel, and he will be my servant forever.”
verses.after: Achish trusted David. “He has made himself a stench to his people Israel,” he thought. “He will be my servant forever.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Achish trusted David, saying, “He has surely made himself odious among his people Israel, and he shall be my servant forever.”

verses.rationale: Preserves the emphatic demand and David’s military predicament.
verses.before: And it happened in those days that the Philistines gathered their camps as an army for battle, to fight against Israel. Achish said to David, “Know for certain that you will go out with me in the camp, you and your men.”
verses.after: In those days the Philistines gathered their armies to fight Israel. Achish told David, “Understand this: you and your men will go out with me in the army.”
verses.tsw_comparator: And it happened in those days that the Philistines gathered their camps as an army for battle, to fight against Israel. Achish said to David, “Know for certain that you shall go out with me in the camp, you and your men.”

verses.rationale: Keeps David’s noncommittal reply and the guard-of-my-head promise.
verses.before: David said to Achish, “Therefore you will know what your servant will do.” Achish said to David, “Therefore I will appoint you keeper of my head all the days.”
verses.after: David answered, “Then you will see what your servant can do.” Achish said, “Then I will make you my bodyguard for life.”
verses.tsw_comparator: David said to Achish, “Therefore you shall know what your servant will do.” Achish said to David, “Therefore I will appoint you keeper of my head all the days.”

verses.rationale: Keeps the repeated death notice and ban as background to the scene.
verses.before: Now Samuel had died, and all Israel had mourned for him and buried him in Ramah, in his city. And Saul had removed the mediums and the spiritists from the land.
verses.after: Samuel had died. All Israel had mourned him and buried him in his hometown of Ramah. Saul had removed the mediums and spiritists from the land.
verses.tsw_comparator: Now Samuel had died, and all Israel had mourned for him and buried him in Ramah, in his city. And Saul had removed the mediums and the spiritists from the land.

verses.rationale: Preserves opposing locations and parallel mobilization.
verses.before: The Philistines gathered, came, and camped at Shunem. Saul gathered all Israel, and they camped at Gilboa.
verses.after: The Philistines gathered and camped at Shunem. Saul gathered all Israel and camped at Gilboa.
verses.tsw_comparator: The Philistines gathered, came, and camped at Shunem. Saul gathered all Israel, and they camped at Gilboa.

verses.rationale: Keeps fear and bodily heart image.
verses.before: When Saul saw the camp of the Philistines, he was afraid, and his heart trembled greatly.
verses.after: When Saul saw the Philistine camp, he was afraid, and his heart trembled violently.
verses.tsw_comparator: When Saul saw the camp of the Philistines, he was afraid, and his heart trembled greatly.

verses.rationale: Retains all three avenues and lack of answer.
verses.before: Saul inquired of the LORD, but the LORD did not answer him, either by dreams, by the Urim, or by prophets.
verses.after: Saul inquired of the LORD, but the LORD did not answer him—not through dreams, Urim, or prophets.
verses.tsw_comparator: Saul inquired of the LORD, but the LORD did not answer him, either by dreams, by the Urim, or by prophets.

verses.rationale: Keeps the woman’s role and Saul’s agency without calling her a witch.
verses.before: Then Saul said to his servants, “Seek for me a woman who is a medium, and I will go to her and inquire through her.” His servants said to him, “Look, there is a woman who is a medium at En-Dor.”
verses.after: Saul told his servants, “Find me a woman who is a medium. I will go and consult her.” They answered, “There is such a woman at En-dor.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Saul said to his servants, “Seek for me a woman who is a medium, and I will go to her and inquire through her.” His servants said to him, “Look, there is a woman who is a medium at En-Dor.”

verses.rationale: Preserves disguise, companions, night and requested act.
verses.before: Saul disguised himself and put on other garments and went, he and two men with him. They came to the woman by night. He said, “Please practice divination for me by a spirit and bring up for me the one whom I say to you.”
verses.after: Saul disguised himself in different clothes and went with two men. They came to the woman at night. He said, “Use your spirit-divination for me and bring up the one I name.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Saul disguised himself and put on other garments and went, he and two men with him. They came to the woman by night. He said, “Please practice divination for me by a spirit and bring up for me the one whom I say to you.”

verses.rationale: Keeps her fear of entrapment and actual death threat.
verses.before: The woman said to him, “Look, you know what Saul has done, how he cut off the mediums and the spiritists from the land. Why then are you laying a trap for my life to put me to death?”
verses.after: The woman answered, “You know what Saul has done. He has cut off the mediums and spiritists from the land. Why are you setting a trap for my life, to have me killed?”
verses.tsw_comparator: The woman said to him, “Look, you know what Saul has done, how he cut off the mediums and the spiritists from the land. Why then are you laying a trap for my life to put me to death?”

verses.rationale: Preserves ironic divine oath and guilt rather than importing an official pardon.
verses.before: Saul swore to her by the LORD, saying, “As the LORD lives, no guilt will happen to you in this matter.”
verses.after: Saul swore to her by the LORD: “As the LORD lives, no guilt will fall on you for this.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Saul swore to her by the LORD, saying, “As the LORD lives, no guilt shall happen to you in this matter.”

verses.rationale: Keeps direct naming and raising language.
verses.before: Then the woman said, “Whom will I bring up for you?” He said, “Bring up Samuel for me.”
verses.after: “Whom shall I bring up for you?” she asked. “Bring up Samuel,” he answered.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the woman said, “Whom shall I bring up for you?” He said, “Bring up Samuel for me.”

verses.rationale: Preserves narrator’s identification as Samuel without imposing fraud or a demon explanation.
verses.before: When the woman saw Samuel, she cried out with a loud voice. The woman said to Saul, “Why have you deceived me? You are Saul!”
verses.after: When the woman saw Samuel, she cried out loudly. “Why have you deceived me?” she said to Saul. “You are Saul!”
verses.tsw_comparator: When the woman saw Samuel, she cried out with a loud voice. The woman said to Saul, “Why have you deceived me? You are Saul!”

verses.rationale: Uses contextual singular for elohim with plural participle, noting the source ambiguity.
verses.before: The king said to her, “Do not be afraid. What did you see?” The woman said to Saul, “I saw a divine being coming up from the earth.”
verses.after: The king said, “Do not be afraid. What do you see?” She answered, “I see a divine being coming up from the earth.”
verses.tsw_comparator: The king said to her, “Do not be afraid. What did you see?” The woman said to Saul, “I saw a divine being coming up from the earth.”

verses.rationale: Preserves Saul’s recognition through description rather than saying he directly saw Samuel.
verses.before: He said to her, “What is his appearance?” She said, “An old man is coming up, and he is wrapped in a robe.” Saul knew that it was Samuel, and he bowed with his face to the ground and prostrated himself.
verses.after: “What does he look like?” he asked. “An old man is coming up, wrapped in a robe,” she said. Saul knew it was Samuel and bowed facedown to the ground.
verses.tsw_comparator: He said to her, “What is his appearance?” She said, “An old man is coming up, and he is wrapped in a robe.” Saul knew that it was Samuel, and he bowed with his face to the ground and prostrated himself.

verses.rationale: Keeps Samuel’s complaint and Saul’s account, including omission of Urim here.
verses.before: Samuel said to Saul, “Why have you disturbed me by bringing me up?” Saul said, “I am in great distress. The Philistines are fighting against me, and God has turned away from me and no longer answers me, either by prophets or by dreams. So I called you to reveal to me what I should do.”
verses.after: Samuel asked Saul, “Why have you disturbed me by bringing me up?” Saul answered, “I am in great distress. The Philistines are fighting me, and God has left me. He no longer answers through prophets or dreams. So I called you to tell me what to do.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Samuel said to Saul, “Why have you disturbed me by bringing me up?” Saul said, “I am in great distress. The Philistines are fighting against me, and God has turned away from me and no longer answers me, either by prophets or by dreams. So I called you to make known to me what I should do.”

verses.rationale: Preserves divine opposition rather than reducing it to absence.
verses.before: Samuel said, “Why then do you ask me, since the LORD has turned away from you and has become your adversary?
verses.after: Samuel said, “Why ask me, when the LORD has left you and become your adversary?
verses.tsw_comparator: Samuel said, “Why then do you ask me, since the LORD has turned away from you and has become your adversary?

verses.rationale: Retains difficult for-himself pronoun reading and explicit naming of David.
verses.before: The LORD has done for himself just as he spoke by my hand. The LORD has torn the kingdom from your hand and given it to your companion, to David.
verses.after: The LORD has acted for himself as he said through me. He has torn the kingdom from your hand and given it to your neighbor, David.
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD has done for himself just as he spoke by my hand. The LORD has torn the kingdom from your hand and given it to your companion, to David.

verses.rationale: Keeps the hearing-voice link to chapter 15 and fierce-anger claim.
verses.before: Because you did not listen to the voice of the LORD and did not carry out his burning anger against Amalek, therefore the LORD has done this thing to you this day.
verses.after: You did not listen to the LORD’s voice or carry out his fierce anger against Amalek. That is why he has done this to you today.
verses.tsw_comparator: Because you did not listen to the voice of the LORD and did not carry out his burning anger against Amalek, therefore the LORD has done this thing to you this day.

verses.rationale: Retains death prediction and with-me language without specifying an afterlife destination.
verses.before: Moreover, the LORD will give Israel with you into the hand of the Philistines. Tomorrow you and your sons will be with me. The LORD will also give the camp of Israel into the hand of the Philistines.”
verses.after: The LORD will hand over Israel along with you to the Philistines. Tomorrow you and your sons will be with me. The LORD will also hand Israel’s army over to the Philistines.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Moreover, the LORD will give Israel with you into the hand of the Philistines. Tomorrow you and your sons shall be with me. The LORD will also give the camp of Israel into the hand of the Philistines.”

verses.rationale: Keeps physical collapse and both fear and fasting as stated factors.
verses.before: Saul hurried and fell full length upon the ground and was very afraid because of Samuel’s words. There was also no strength in him, for he had eaten no bread all that day and all that night.
verses.after: Saul immediately fell full length to the ground, terrified by Samuel’s words. He had no strength left, for he had eaten nothing all that day and night.
verses.tsw_comparator: Saul hurried and fell full length upon the ground and was very afraid because of Samuel’s words. There was also no strength in him, for he had eaten no bread all that day and all that night.

verses.rationale: Preserves her claimed obedience and risk, echoing the hearing motif.
verses.before: The woman came to Saul and saw that he was greatly terrified. She said to him, “Look, your female servant listened to your voice. I placed my life in my hand and listened to your words that you spoke to me.
verses.after: The woman came to Saul and saw how shaken he was. She said, “Your servant listened to your voice. I took my life in my hands and did what you told me.
verses.tsw_comparator: The woman came to Saul and saw that he was greatly terrified. She said to him, “Look, your female servant listened to your voice. I placed my life in my hand and listened to your words that you spoke to me.

verses.rationale: Keeps reciprocal listening and practical hospitality.
verses.before: And now, please, you also listen to the voice of your female servant, and let me set before you a morsel of bread. Eat, so that there may be strength in you when you go on your way.”
verses.after: Now please listen to your servant’s voice. Let me set a little bread before you. Eat, so you will have strength for the journey.”
verses.tsw_comparator: And now, please, you also listen to the voice of your female servant, and let me set before you a morsel of bread. Eat, so that there may be strength in you when you go on your way.”

verses.rationale: Preserves refusal, persuasion and changed posture.
verses.before: But he refused and said, “I will not eat.” His servants and the woman pressed him, and he listened to their voice. He arose from the ground and sat on the bed.
verses.after: He refused. “I will not eat.” But his servants and the woman pressed him, and he listened to them. He got up from the ground and sat on the bed.
verses.tsw_comparator: But he refused and said, “I will not eat.” His servants and the woman pressed him, and he listened to their voice. He arose from the ground and sat on the bed.

verses.rationale: Keeps the costly meal and all preparation steps.
verses.before: The woman had a fattened calf in the house, and she hurried and slaughtered it. She took flour, kneaded it, and baked unleavened bread from it.
verses.after: The woman had a fattened calf at home. She quickly slaughtered it, took flour, kneaded it, and baked unleavened bread.
verses.tsw_comparator: The woman had a fattened calf in the house, and she hurried and slaughtered it. She took flour, kneaded it, and baked unleavened bread from it.

verses.rationale: Preserves meal and return to darkness without a sermon ending.
verses.before: She brought it before Saul and before his servants, and they ate. Then they arose and went away that night.
verses.after: She served Saul and his servants, and they ate. Then they rose and left that same night.
verses.tsw_comparator: She brought it before Saul and before his servants, and they ate. Then they arose and went away that night.

verses.rationale: Keeps the different staging locations without harmonizing chapter 28’s scene order.
verses.before: The Philistines gathered all their camps at Aphek, while Israel camped by the spring that is in Jezreel.
verses.after: The Philistines gathered all their armies at Aphek, while Israel camped by the spring at Jezreel.
verses.tsw_comparator: The Philistines gathered all their camps at Aphek, while Israel camped by the spring that is in Jezreel.

verses.rationale: Retains ordered units and David’s position.
verses.before: The rulers of the Philistines were passing by according to hundreds and thousands, and David and his men were passing at the rear with Achish.
verses.after: The Philistine rulers marched past in hundreds and thousands. David and his men came at the rear with Achish.
verses.tsw_comparator: The rulers of the Philistines were passing by according to hundreds and thousands, and David and his men were passing at the rear with Achish.

verses.rationale: Preserves Achish’s imprecise days-or-years expression without adding an explicit self-correction; his confidence remains his assessment.
verses.before: Then the commanders of the Philistines said, “What are these Hebrews?” Achish said to the commanders of the Philistines, “Is this not David, servant of Saul king of Israel, who has been with me these days or these years? I have found nothing against him from the day he fell away to me until this day.”
verses.after: The Philistine commanders asked, “What are these Hebrews doing here?” Achish answered, “This is David, servant of Saul king of Israel. He has been with me these days or these years—and I have found no fault in him from the day he came over until now.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the commanders of the Philistines said, “What are these Hebrews?” Achish said to the commanders of the Philistines, “Is this not David, servant of Saul king of Israel, who has been with me these days or these years? I have found nothing against him from the day he fell away to me until this day.”

verses.rationale: Keeps adversary as a human military role and the beheading threat.
verses.before: But the commanders of the Philistines became angry with him. The commanders of the Philistines said to him, “Send the man back, and let him return to his place where you assigned him. Let him not go down with us into battle, lest he become an adversary to us in the battle. For with what could this one reconcile himself to his lord? Would it not be with the heads of these men?
verses.after: The commanders were angry with Achish. “Send the man back to the place you assigned him,” they said. “He must not go into battle with us and become our adversary. How better could he regain his master’s favor than with these men’s heads?
verses.tsw_comparator: But the commanders of the Philistines became angry with him. The commanders of the Philistines said to him, “Send the man back, and let him return to his place where you assigned him. Let him not go down with us into battle, lest he become an adversary to us in the battle. For with what could this one reconcile himself to his lord? Would it not be with the heads of these men?

verses.rationale: Repeats the same song exactly, keeping its political effect visible.
verses.before: Is this not David, concerning whom they answered in dances, saying: ‘Saul has struck his thousands, and David his ten thousands’?”
verses.after: Is this not the David they sang about as they danced: ‘Saul has struck down his thousands, and David his tens of thousands’?”
verses.tsw_comparator: Is this not David, concerning whom they answered in dances, saying: ‘Saul has struck his thousands, and David his ten thousands’?”

verses.rationale: Preserves Achish’s oath by the LORD and his assessment as speech.
verses.before: Then Achish called David and said to him, “As the LORD lives, you have been upright, and your going out and your coming in with me in the camp are good in my eyes. I have not found evil in you from the day of your coming to me until this day. Even so, in the eyes of the rulers you are not good.
verses.after: Achish called David and said, “As the LORD lives, you have been upright. I have been pleased to have you go out and come in with me in the army. I have found no evil in you since you came to me, but the rulers do not approve of you.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Achish called David and said to him, “As the LORD lives, you have been upright, and your going out and your coming in with me in the camp are good in my eyes. I have not found evil in you from the day of your coming to me until this day. Nevertheless, in the eyes of the rulers you are not good.

verses.rationale: Keeps peaceful dismissal and caution.
verses.before: And now return and go in peace, so that you do not do what is evil in the eyes of the rulers of the Philistines.”
verses.after: Now turn back and go in peace. Do nothing to displease the Philistine rulers.”
verses.tsw_comparator: And now return and go in peace, so that you do not do what is evil in the eyes of the rulers of the Philistines.”

verses.rationale: Preserves ambiguous loyalty in David’s protest without revealing an unspoken plan.
verses.before: David said to Achish, “But what have I done? And what have you found in your servant from the day that I have been before you until this day, that I should not go and fight against the enemies of my lord the king?”
verses.after: David asked, “But what have I done? What fault have you found in your servant all the time I have been with you, that I cannot go and fight the enemies of my lord the king?”
verses.tsw_comparator: David said to Achish, “But what have I done? And what have you found in your servant from the day that I have been before you until this day, that I should not go and fight against the enemies of my lord the king?”

verses.rationale: Keeps messenger comparison and contrast with commanders’ decision.
verses.before: Achish answered and said to David, “I know that you are good in my eyes like a messenger of God. Even so, the commanders of the Philistines have said, ‘He will not go up with us into the battle.’
verses.after: Achish answered, “I know. To me you are as good as a messenger of God. But the Philistine commanders have said, ‘He must not go to battle with us.’
verses.tsw_comparator: Achish answered and said to David, “I know that you are good in my eyes like a messenger of God. Nevertheless, the commanders of the Philistines have said, ‘He shall not go up with us into the battle.’

verses.rationale: Preserves your-master designation and repeated early departure.
verses.before: And now rise early in the morning, you and the servants of your lord who came with you. Rise early in the morning, and when you have light, go.”
verses.after: Get up early tomorrow with your master’s servants who came with you. Rise early, and leave as soon as it is light.”
verses.tsw_comparator: And now rise early in the morning, you and the servants of your lord who came with you. Rise early in the morning, and when you have light, go.”

verses.rationale: Keeps divergent movements and David’s removal from the battle.
verses.before: So David arose early, he and his men, to go in the morning to return to the land of the Philistines. And the Philistines went up to Jezreel.
verses.after: David and his men got up early to return to Philistine territory, while the Philistines went up to Jezreel.
verses.tsw_comparator: So David arose early, he and his men, to go in the morning to return to the land of the Philistines. And the Philistines went up to Jezreel.

verses.rationale: Keeps third day and the retrospective account of the raid.
verses.before: And it happened when David and his men came to Ziklag on the third day that the Amalekites had raided the Negev and Ziklag. They had struck Ziklag and burned it with fire.
verses.after: David and his men reached Ziklag on the third day. The Amalekites had raided the Negeb and Ziklag, attacked the town, and burned it down.
verses.tsw_comparator: And it happened when David and his men came to Ziklag on the third day that the Amalekites had raided the Negev and Ziklag. They had struck Ziklag and burned it with fire.

verses.rationale: Preserves the women named and comprehensive small/great scope, distinct from David’s earlier raids.
verses.before: They took captive the women who were in it, from small to great. They did not put anyone to death, but carried them away and went on their way.
verses.after: They had taken the women there captive, along with everyone from small to great. They had killed no one, but driven them away and gone on.
verses.tsw_comparator: They took captive the women who were in it, from small to great. They did not put anyone to death, but carried them away and went on their way.

verses.rationale: Keeps all three family groups and the discovery viewpoint.
verses.before: David and his men came to the city, and look, it was burned with fire, and their wives, sons, and daughters had been taken captive.
verses.after: David and his men came to the town and found it burned down. Their wives, sons, and daughters had been taken captive.
verses.tsw_comparator: David and his men came to the city, and behold, it was burned with fire, and their wives, sons, and daughters had been taken captive.

verses.rationale: Preserves unrestrained collective grief and its bodily exhaustion.
verses.before: Then David and the people who were with him lifted their voices and wept until there was no strength in them to weep.
verses.after: David and the men with him wept aloud until they had no strength left to weep.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then David and the people who were with him lifted their voices and wept until there was no strength in them to weep.

verses.rationale: Retains repeated names and Abigail’s previous marriage identification.
verses.before: David’s two wives had been taken captive, Ahinoam the Jezreelite and Abigail wife of Nabal the Carmelite.
verses.after: David’s two wives had been taken too: Ahinoam of Jezreel and Abigail, the wife of Nabal of Carmel.
verses.tsw_comparator: David’s two wives had been taken captive, Ahinoam the Jezreelite and Abigail wife of Nabal the Carmelite.

verses.rationale: Keeps threat from his own men, qere sons and contrasting renewed strength.
verses.before: David was greatly distressed, for the people said to stone him, because the life of all the people was bitter, each over his sons and daughters. But David strengthened himself in the LORD his God.
verses.after: David was in great distress. The men talked of stoning him, bitter in spirit over their sons and daughters. But David found strength in the LORD his God.
verses.tsw_comparator: David was greatly distressed, for the people said to stone him, because the life of all the people was bitter, each over his sons and daughters. But David strengthened himself in the LORD his God.

verses.rationale: Preserves full priestly identification and fulfilled request.
verses.before: David said to Abiathar the priest, son of Ahimelech, “Please bring near to me the ephod.” Abiathar brought the ephod near to David.
verses.after: He told Abiathar the priest, son of Ahimelech, “Bring me the ephod.” Abiathar brought it to him.
verses.tsw_comparator: David said to Abiathar the priest, son of Ahimelech, “Please bring near to me the ephod.” Abiathar brought the ephod near to David.

verses.rationale: Keeps two questions and emphatic double assurance; captives makes the rescue object clear.
verses.before: David inquired of the LORD, saying, “Will I pursue after this raiding band? Will I overtake them?” He said to him, “Pursue, for you will surely overtake and surely rescue.”
verses.after: David inquired of the LORD, “Should I pursue this raiding band? Will I overtake them?” The answer came, “Pursue them. You will surely overtake them and surely rescue the captives.”
verses.tsw_comparator: David inquired of the LORD, saying, “Shall I pursue after this raiding band? Will I overtake them?” He said to him, “Pursue, for you shall surely overtake and surely rescue.”

verses.rationale: Preserves initial force and the location of separation.
verses.before: So David went, he and the six hundred men who were with him, and they came to the Wadi Besor. People who were left behind remained.
verses.after: David set out with his six hundred men. They reached the Wadi Besor, where some stayed behind.
verses.tsw_comparator: So David went, he and the six hundred men who were with him, and they came to the Wadi Besor. Those who were left behind remained.

verses.rationale: Keeps exhaustion as reason and exact division of the force.
verses.before: David pursued, he and four hundred men, but two hundred remained behind, who were too exhausted to cross the Wadi Besor.
verses.after: David continued the pursuit with four hundred men. Two hundred were too exhausted to cross the Wadi Besor and stayed there.
verses.tsw_comparator: David pursued, he and four hundred men, but two hundred remained behind, who were too exhausted to cross the Wadi Besor.

verses.rationale: Retains aid before interrogation and the man’s nationality.
verses.before: They found an Egyptian man in the field and took him to David. They gave him bread, and he ate, and they gave him water to drink.
verses.after: They found an Egyptian in the open country and brought him to David. They gave him bread to eat and water to drink.
verses.tsw_comparator: They found an Egyptian man in the field and took him to David. They gave him bread, and he ate, and they gave him water to drink.

verses.rationale: Preserves food quantities, exact deprivation and revived-spirit image.
verses.before: They gave him a piece of a fig cake and two clusters of raisins. He ate, and his spirit returned to him, for he had eaten no bread and drunk no water for three days and three nights.
verses.after: They also gave him part of a fig cake and two raisin cakes. He ate, and his spirit returned. He had eaten no bread and drunk no water for three days and three nights.
verses.tsw_comparator: They gave him a piece of a fig cake and two clusters of raisins. He ate, and his spirit returned to him, for he had eaten no bread and drunk no water for three days and three nights.

verses.rationale: Retains enslavement and abandonment rather than employment language.
verses.before: David said to him, “To whom do you belong, and from where are you?” He said, “I am an Egyptian young man, servant to an Amalekite man. My master abandoned me because I became sick three days ago.
verses.after: David asked, “Whom do you belong to, and where are you from?” He answered, “I am an Egyptian youth, a slave of an Amalekite. My master abandoned me when I fell ill three days ago.
verses.tsw_comparator: David said to him, “To whom do you belong, and from where are you?” He said, “I am an Egyptian young man, servant to an Amalekite man. My master abandoned me because I became sick three days ago.

verses.rationale: Keeps all raid areas and the speaker’s participation.
verses.before: We raided the Negev of the Cherethites, what belongs to Judah, and the Negev of Caleb, and we burned Ziklag with fire.”
verses.after: We raided the Negeb of the Cherethites, the territory of Judah, and the Negeb of Caleb. We burned Ziklag down.”
verses.tsw_comparator: We raided the Negev of the Cherethites, what belongs to Judah, and the Negev of Caleb, and we burned Ziklag with fire.”

verses.rationale: Preserves the enslaved man’s two protective conditions.
verses.before: David said to him, “Will you bring me down to this raiding band?” He said, “Swear to me by God that you will not put me to death and will not deliver me into the hand of my master, and I will bring you down to this raiding band.”
verses.after: David asked, “Will you lead me down to this raiding band?” He answered, “Swear to me by God that you will not kill me or hand me back to my master. Then I will lead you to them.”
verses.tsw_comparator: David said to him, “Will you bring me down to this raiding band?” He said, “Swear to me by God that you will not put me to death and will not deliver me into the hand of my master, and I will bring you down to this raiding band.”

verses.rationale: Keeps discovery, celebration and both lands plundered.
verses.before: He brought him down, and look, they were spread over all the face of the land, eating, drinking, and celebrating because of all the great spoil that they had taken from the land of the Philistines and from the land of Judah.
verses.after: He led David down. There they were, scattered across the countryside, eating, drinking, and celebrating all the great plunder they had taken from Philistine territory and Judah.
verses.tsw_comparator: He brought him down, and behold, they were spread over all the face of the land, eating, drinking, and celebrating because of all the great spoil that they had taken from the land of the Philistines and from the land of Judah.

verses.rationale: Retains ambiguous twilight timing and exact number and means of escape.
verses.before: David struck them from twilight until the evening of the next day. Not a man from them escaped except four hundred young men who rode on camels and fled.
verses.after: David struck them from twilight until the next evening. No one escaped except four hundred young men who rode off on camels.
verses.tsw_comparator: David struck them from twilight until the evening of the next day. Not a man from them escaped except four hundred young men who rode on camels and fled.

verses.rationale: Keeps comprehensive rescue and specific wives.
verses.before: David rescued all that the Amalekites had taken, and David rescued his two wives.
verses.after: David rescued everything the Amalekites had taken, including his two wives.
verses.tsw_comparator: David rescued all that the Amalekites had taken, and David rescued his two wives.

verses.rationale: Preserves comprehensive repetition and both genders among children.
verses.before: Nothing of theirs was missing, from small to great, sons or daughters, from spoil or anything that they had taken for themselves. David brought back everything.
verses.after: Nothing was missing, small or great—sons, daughters, plunder, or anything they had taken. David brought it all back.
verses.tsw_comparator: Nothing of theirs was missing, from small to great, sons or daughters, from spoil or anything that they had taken for themselves. David brought back everything.

verses.rationale: Keeps the difficult livestock distinction without inventing owners; note flags the wording.
verses.before: David took all the sheep and cattle. They drove them before that livestock and said, “This is David’s spoil.”
verses.after: He took all the sheep and cattle. His men drove them ahead of the other livestock, saying, “This is David’s plunder.”
verses.tsw_comparator: David took all the sheep and cattle. They drove them before that livestock and said, “This is David’s spoil.”

verses.rationale: Preserves exhausted men’s welcome and David’s reciprocal greeting.
verses.before: David came to the two hundred men who had been too exhausted to follow David and whom they had made stay at the Wadi Besor. They went out to meet David and to meet the people who were with him. David drew near to the people and asked about their well-being.
verses.after: David came back to the two hundred men who had been too exhausted to follow and had been left at the Wadi Besor. They came out to meet him and his men. David approached and greeted them.
verses.tsw_comparator: David came to the two hundred men who had been too exhausted to follow David and whom they had made stay at the Wadi Besor. They went out to meet David and to meet the people who were with him. David drew near to the people and asked about their well-being.

verses.rationale: Keeps narrator’s evaluation and the exclusionary proposal as quoted speech.
verses.before: Then every evil and worthless man from among the men who had gone with David answered and said, “Because they did not go with us, we will not give them from the spoil that we rescued, except to each man his wife and his children, so that they may lead them away and go.”
verses.after: But all the wicked, worthless men among those who had gone with David said, “They did not come with us. We will give them none of the plunder we rescued. Each can take only his wife and children and leave.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Then every evil and worthless man from among the men who had gone with David answered and said, “Because they did not go with us, we will not give them from the spoil that we rescued, except to each man his wife and his children, so that they may lead them away and go.”

verses.rationale: Preserves brothers address and gift/protection as reasons for sharing.
verses.before: Yet David said, “You will not do so, my brothers, with what the LORD has given us. He guarded us and gave into our hand the raiding band that came against us.
verses.after: David said, “My brothers, you must not do that with what the LORD has given us. He protected us and handed over the band that attacked us.
verses.tsw_comparator: But David said, “You shall not do so, my brothers, with what the LORD has given us. He guarded us and gave into our hand the raiding band that came against us.

verses.rationale: Keeps equal shares and both roles without recasting exhausted men as deserters.
verses.before: And who will listen to you in this matter? For as the share of the one who goes down into battle, so will be the share of the one who remains with the baggage. They will share alike.”
verses.after: Who would listen to such a proposal? The share of the one who goes into battle will be the same as the share of the one who stays with the supplies. They will share alike.”
verses.tsw_comparator: And who will listen to you in this matter? For as the share of the one who goes down into battle, so shall be the share of the one who remains with the baggage. They shall share alike.”

verses.rationale: Retains paired legal terms and narrator’s temporal viewpoint.
verses.before: And it happened from that day and onward that he made it a statute and judgment for Israel to this day.
verses.after: From that day forward he made this a statute and rule for Israel, and it remains so to this day.
verses.tsw_comparator: And it happened from that day and onward that he made it a statute and judgment for Israel to this day.

verses.rationale: Keeps gift as blessing and the recipients’ political/friendship roles.
verses.before: David came to Ziklag and sent some of the spoil to the elders of Judah, to his companions, saying, “Look, a blessing for you from the spoil of the enemies of the LORD”—
verses.after: When David reached Ziklag, he sent some of the plunder to his friends, the elders of Judah: “Here is a blessing for you from the plunder of the LORD’s enemies.”
verses.tsw_comparator: David came to Ziklag and sent some of the spoil to the elders of Judah, to his companions, saying, “Look, a blessing for you from the spoil of the enemies of the LORD”—

verses.rationale: Preserves first three place names with the list continuing.
verses.before: to those in Bethel, those in Ramoth of the Negev, those in Jattir,
verses.after: He sent it to those in Bethel, Ramoth-negeb, and Jattir;
verses.tsw_comparator: to those in Bethel, those in Ramoth of the Negev, those in Jattir,

verses.rationale: Retains all three locations without omissions.
verses.before: those in Aroer, those in Siphmoth, those in Eshtemoa,
verses.after: to those in Aroer, Siphmoth, and Eshtemoa;
verses.tsw_comparator: those in Aroer, those in Siphmoth, those in Eshtemoa,

verses.rationale: Keeps pinned Racal and distinct clan settlements.
verses.before: those in Racal, those in the cities of the Jerahmeelites, those in the cities of the Kenites,
verses.after: to those in Racal, the Jerahmeelite towns, and the Kenite towns;
verses.tsw_comparator: those in Racal, those in the cities of the Jerahmeelites, those in the cities of the Kenites,

verses.rationale: Preserves the three named recipients’ towns.
verses.before: those in Hormah, those in Bor-Ashan, those in Athach,
verses.after: to those in Hormah, Bor-ashan, and Athach;
verses.tsw_comparator: those in Hormah, those in Bor-Ashan, those in Athach,

verses.rationale: Closes the gift list with both specific Hebron and wider scope.
verses.before: those in Hebron, and to all the places where David and his men had walked.
verses.after: to those in Hebron and all the places where David and his men had roamed.
verses.tsw_comparator: those in Hebron, and to all the places where David and his men had walked.

verses.rationale: Keeps the simultaneous battle thread and defeat location.
verses.before: The Philistines fought against Israel, and the men of Israel fled from before the Philistines and fell slain on Mount Gilboa.
verses.after: The Philistines were fighting Israel. The Israelites fled before them and fell slain on Mount Gilboa.
verses.tsw_comparator: The Philistines fought against Israel, and the men of Israel fled from before the Philistines and fell slain on Mount Gilboa.

verses.rationale: Preserves all three names without harmonizing Abinadab with chapter 14’s list.
verses.before: The Philistines pressed hard after Saul and after his sons, and the Philistines struck Jonathan, Abinadab, and Malchi-Shua, sons of Saul.
verses.after: The Philistines closed in on Saul and his sons. They killed Jonathan, Abinadab, and Malchi-shua, Saul’s sons.
verses.tsw_comparator: The Philistines pressed hard after Saul and after his sons, and the Philistines struck Jonathan, Abinadab, and Malchi-Shua, sons of Saul.

verses.rationale: Uses stricken to retain the difficult wounded/anguished expression, with alternatives noted.
verses.before: The battle became heavy against Saul. The archers found him, and he was badly wounded by the archers.
verses.after: The battle pressed hard on Saul. The archers found him, and he was badly stricken by them.
verses.tsw_comparator: The battle became heavy against Saul. The archers found him, and he was badly wounded by the archers.

verses.rationale: Preserves self-inflicted death, feared abuse and the armor-bearer’s refusal without euphemism.
verses.before: Then Saul said to his armor-bearer, “Draw your sword and pierce me with it, lest these uncircumcised come and pierce me and abuse me.” But his armor-bearer was not willing, for he was greatly afraid. So Saul took the sword and fell upon it.
verses.after: Saul told his armor-bearer, “Draw your sword and run me through. Otherwise these uncircumcised men will come, run me through, and abuse me.” His armor-bearer refused, for he was terrified. So Saul took his sword and fell on it.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Saul said to his armor-bearer, “Draw your sword and pierce me with it, lest these uncircumcised come and pierce me and abuse me.” But his armor-bearer was not willing, for he was greatly afraid. So Saul took the sword and fell upon it.

verses.rationale: Retains Saul already dead and the second suicide as narrator statements.
verses.before: When his armor-bearer saw that Saul was dead, he also fell upon his sword and died with him.
verses.after: When the armor-bearer saw that Saul was dead, he too fell on his sword and died with him.
verses.tsw_comparator: When his armor-bearer saw that Saul was dead, he also fell upon his sword and died with him.

verses.rationale: Preserves the narrator’s comprehensive summary without silently restricting all.
verses.before: So Saul died, and his three sons, and his armor-bearer, and all his men, together on that day.
verses.after: So Saul, his three sons, his armor-bearer, and all his men died together that day.
verses.tsw_comparator: So Saul died, and his three sons, and his armor-bearer, and all his men, together on that day.

verses.rationale: Keeps both geographic groups and displacement followed by occupation.
verses.before: When the men of Israel who were on the other side of the valley and people who were beyond the Jordan saw that the men of Israel had fled and that Saul and his sons were dead, they abandoned the cities and fled. Then the Philistines came and lived in them.
verses.after: The Israelites across the valley and beyond the Jordan saw that Israel’s men had fled and Saul and his sons were dead. They abandoned their towns and fled, and the Philistines came and settled in them.
verses.tsw_comparator: When the men of Israel who were on the other side of the valley and those who were beyond the Jordan saw that the men of Israel had fled and that Saul and his sons were dead, they abandoned the cities and fled. Then the Philistines came and lived in them.

verses.rationale: Preserves next-day timing and purpose of stripping corpses.
verses.before: And it happened the next day when the Philistines came to strip the slain that they found Saul and his three sons fallen on Mount Gilboa.
verses.after: The next day the Philistines came to strip the dead. They found Saul and his three sons fallen on Mount Gilboa.
verses.tsw_comparator: And it happened the next day when the Philistines came to strip the slain that they found Saul and his three sons fallen on Mount Gilboa.

verses.rationale: Keeps desecration and cultic/public announcement without importing another account’s details.
verses.before: They cut off his head and stripped off his weapons and sent throughout the land of the Philistines all around to proclaim the news in the houses of their idols and among the people.
verses.after: They cut off Saul’s head and stripped away his armor. They sent word throughout Philistine territory to announce the news in their idols’ temples and among the people.
verses.tsw_comparator: They cut off his head and stripped off his weapons and sent throughout the land of the Philistines all around to proclaim the news in the houses of their idols and among the people.

verses.rationale: Retains named sanctuary and public display of the body.
verses.before: They put his weapons in the house of the Ashtaroth and fastened his body to the wall of Beth-Shan.
verses.after: They placed his armor in the temple of Ashtaroth and fastened his body to the wall of Beth-shan.
verses.tsw_comparator: They put his weapons in the house of the Ashtaroth and fastened his body to the wall of Beth-Shan.

verses.rationale: Keeps the community linked to Saul’s earlier rescue without adding explanation to the verse.
verses.before: When the inhabitants of Jabesh-Gilead heard concerning him what the Philistines had done to Saul,
verses.after: The people of Jabesh-gilead heard what the Philistines had done to Saul.
verses.tsw_comparator: When the inhabitants of Jabesh-Gilead heard concerning him what the Philistines had done to Saul,

verses.rationale: Preserves recovery, night journey and actual burning rather than substituting burial only.
verses.before: all the valiant men arose and walked all night. They took the body of Saul and the bodies of his sons from the wall of Beth-Shan, came to Jabesh, and burned them there.
verses.after: All their fighting men set out and traveled all night. They took the bodies of Saul and his sons from Beth-shan’s wall, brought them to Jabesh, and burned them there.
verses.tsw_comparator: all the valiant men arose and walked all night. They took the body of Saul and the bodies of his sons from the wall of Beth-Shan, came to Jabesh, and burned them there.

verses.rationale: Keeps bones, tree, place and exact mourning duration.
verses.before: They took their bones and buried them under the tamarisk tree at Jabesh, and they fasted seven days.
verses.after: They took the bones and buried them under the tamarisk at Jabesh. Then they fasted for seven days.
verses.tsw_comparator: They took their bones and buried them under the tamarisk tree at Jabesh, and they fasted seven days.
